Develop comprehensive performance dashboards that track real-time metrics including Activity KPIs, Pipeline Health, and Win/Loss ratios. Partner with Sales Leadership to design and implement strategic initiatives such as territory mapping, quota setting and performance analysis.

Design, organize and lead sales enablement sessions with sales team stakeholders to ensure alignment on strategic plays and best practices. Facilitate the Marketing-to-Sales handoff by managing lead scoring and routing logic to ensure every MQL is followed up on in a timely manner.

Build predictive forecasting models by analyzing historical trends and seasonal data to project monthly and quarterly revenue targets. You are comfortable navigating complex back-end settings, creating custom objects, and managing third-party integrations to keep the sales engine running smoothly. Analytical Mindset and Data Storytelling: You have a natural ability to turn raw numbers into a narrative.

You are highly proficient in Google Sheets (or MS Excel) and have experience using data visualization tools like Tableau, Looker, PowerBI or Hex to help leadership quickly digest trends and performance. Systems Thinking and Problem Solving: You don't just fix symptoms; you look for the root cause.

You understand how a change in the sales workflow might impact marketing data or finance reports, and you enjoy the challenge of building scalable processes that benefit the entire organization. Exceptional Communication and Collaboration: You can translate technical CRM jargon into plain English for sales reps and managers.

You thrive in a cross-functional environment, acting as a bridge between Marketing, Sales, and Finance to ensure everyone is aligned on the same revenue goals. Adaptability and Curiosity: You are energized by a fast-paced, high-growth environment like Kami ’s. Our teams are growing as are our product offerings, so no two days are the same.

You are a lifelong learner who stays up to date on the latest GTM technology trends and is always looking for a more efficient way to get the job done.You are someone who explores and breaks down problems, to solve processes and make systems run more efficiently.

Mission-Driven Focus: You are motivated by the opportunity to support educators and students. You want your work to have a tangible impact on global education, and you take pride in knowing that your operational excellence helps Kami reach more classrooms worldwide. Why Kami ?

We’re building a high performance, best in class team to help capitalize on our exciting momentum, and continue scaling Kami 's magic and making a difference to schools, students, and teachers.

Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet. We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.
Merchandising Operations Manager
Grove's merchandising operation is full of good instincts running on manual work. This role exists to fix that: redesign the core processes, then personally build the automation that makes them stick. This is a rare shot at rebuilding how merchandising actually runs, and at proving AI belongs in the hands of the person closest to the problem, not just the AI team.
We're not hiring someone to write a strategy memo about AI and hand it off. We're hiring someone who will map the workflow, feel where it breaks, and then sit down and build the thing that fixes it.
More About the Opportunity
Merchandising at Grove runs on real expertise and too much manual glue.
Buyers chase vendors for the same data, week after week.
Marketing launches promotions inventory finds out about too late.
Good people spend their time on work a workflow should be doing for them.
We have an internal AI team. They coach. They don't build for you.
This role is for the person who wants their hands on the keyboard, not the person who scopes it and waits.
The honest version: no template here. You're defining the standard as you go, with review at key milestones and real autonomy in between.
Some of what you build will work on the first try. Some won't. That's the job.
What You'll Own
Map how merchandising actually works today, not how the org chart says it works.
Redesign core operating processes for speed, accuracy, and margin protection: assortment planning, item setup, pricing and markdown, vendor and PO management, allocation, replenishment.
Own the calendar connecting marketing activations to inventory, so launches are stock-backed, not a surprise to the warehouse.
Translate activation plans into buy, allocation, and replenishment signals; flag stock risk before launch, not after.
Coordinate vendor commitments tied to activations: fill rates, lead times, launch quantities.
Build self-service tools and proactive alerts that scale the buyer-vendor relationship, including visibility into vendor performance.
Build the automation yourself, using Claude and comparable AI tools, no/low-code platforms, and lightweight automation, from concept through rollout.
Run pilots end to end: scope, build, test for accuracy, validate fit, scale. Keep humans in the loop on margin- and inventory-critical decisions.
Maintain a registry of approved tools and active automations, so what exists and what it's for is never a mystery.
Own change management for every rollout: training, AI literacy for non-technical audiences, office hours, a bench of power users.
Build reporting on process and automation performance, and use it to prioritize what gets built next.

Real fluency in retail merchandising operations, not an adjacent function you've watched from a distance.
You've mapped a broken process and redesigned it, not just diagnosed it.
Basic technical acumen and a genuine willingness to build, no engineering background required.
Comfortable working with a specialist team as a coaching resource, not a build team, and taking their guidance without handing off your job.
You've run a pilot from scoping through adoption, and you know the gap between a demo and something people actually use.
You care about the boring, durable stuff: documentation, SOPs, registries, training, the things that outlast the person who built them.
You think in workflows and root causes, not tickets.
You know the difference between a problem worth automating and one worth leaving alone.
Even Better if You Have
Built something with Claude or a comparable AI tool that a non-technical team now relies on.
Experience connecting marketing or demand planning to inventory and allocation.
Designed a self-service tool that measurably cut manual buyer-vendor back-and-forth.
A retail, CPG, or commerce background with real fluency in vendor and marketplace dynamics.

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.
We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $11B - multiples of 11, always.

s.h: We have expanded from voice into three main platforms
s.t:
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.
Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.
How we work
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.
Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.
Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.
Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

At Foxelli Group , we're not just leading the digital marketplace - we're redefining it. With 10 years of experience and a portfolio of thriving direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands generating over $20 million USD annually, we’re pushing boundaries to achieve our next growth milestone.

That’s why we’re on the hunt for an Operations Manager who’s ready to make a real impact. ❕This role is 100% remote, and you will join a team that already works from 20 different world countries. THE ROLE We’re on a mission to make work smarter, faster , and more impactful .

As an Operations Manager , you’ll be at the heart of our efforts to refine internal processes, resolve inefficiencies, and drive impactful improvements in collaboration with our COO.

This role is perfect for someone who loves to uncover and eliminate the root causes of operational challenges, creating systems that empower teams to work at their best. RESPONSIBILITIES Identify and Fix Inefficiencies: Analyze workflows across teams to uncover inefficiencies, gaps, or breakdowns in communication.

Propose and implement solutions to streamline operations and standardize processes.. Optimize Systems: Oversee and maintain our OKRs system, ensuring it reflects up-to-date data. Lead the migration from Excel to the best-fit OKR platform for our company, creating a seamless transition.

Enhance Collaboration: Establish and improve communication flows to ensure teams are aligned and information is not lost or delayed. This includes summarizing key takeaways from managerial meetings, distilling what truly matters, and transforming insights into clear, actionable leaflets to improve internal communication.

Strategic Initiatives: Work closely with the COO to identify non-functional areas, develop action plans, and drive strategic initiatives that enhance company operations. Root Cause Analysis: Dig deep into recurring challenges to uncover and address underlying issues, preventing future roadblocks.

Requirements SKILLS & EXPERIENCE A natural problem-solver is passionate about optimizing business operations and creating impactful change. Hands-on experience in e-commerce business operations or similar roles. Strong skills in process mapping, workflow visualization, and system improvement.

Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities, with a talent for asking the right questions, gathering insights, and drawing actionable conclusions. Familiarity with OKRs systems and platforms, with experience in transitioning between tools.

Proficiency in tools like Asana (or similar project management platforms) and Excel for data analysis and reporting. A proactive mindset, ready to take ownership of challenges and deliver long-term solutions. Strong leadership and a collaborative mindset. Results-driven with a focus on measurable outcomes.

THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS 10 min online DISC assessment to identify your behavioral style, as we strongly believe in the power of diverse teams. 15-30 min intro e-meet with Foxelli Group CPO to discuss company, role, your experiences, and expectations. 60-90 min e-meet with Foxelli Group board members - CEO, CCO, COO, and CPO to discuss: the vision of the role, your competencies, and technical skills.

Have a both-sided Q&A session. Home Task. Decision & Feedback from us. SALARY €1,500 - €2,500 after taxes, depending on yourskills, competencies, and experience, with the potential for quarterly performance-based bonuses tied to KPIs. ❕Please note that this role requires a self-employment certificate.

PERKS & BENEFITS Complimentary gym memberships and company-sponsored outdoor adventures for your strength and keeping your physical well-being in check. A personal development budget is at your disposal for your personal and professional growth to ensure you keep continuously growing.

Generous paid time off, including parental leave and vacation days, to recharge and rejuvenate and ensure you’re well-rested . A budget for your home office setup so you’re comfortable working how you like and where you like. Strong company culture and a network of unique individuals that celebrates you .

Full flexibility with your schedule in a fully remote setting for your control of a working day, powered by Hubstaff for transparency and fairness. ELIGIBILITY & LOCATION REQUIREMENTS At Foxelli Group, our team operates primarily in the Eastern European Time Zone (EET), which is UTC+2 and UTC+3 .

About Maneva Maneva is an AI services company founded by a former Google DeepMind researcher, focused on transforming manufacturing operations through advanced AI. We enable autonomous factory operation and optimization by generating AI-driven actions and insights using off-the-shelf hardware or existing vision systems.

We've grown rapidly and are well-funded, technically exceptional, and mission-driven. As we grow, we're building a people-first culture that attracts, develops, and retains world-class talent. Role Overview Maneva is seeking a People & Business Operations Manager to build and lead our people operations function at a critical stage of growth.

This role sits at the intersection of employee lifecycle management, governance, business operations, and culture.

You'll own performance management infrastructure, compensation and benefits administration, employee relations, U.S. state-level employment compliance as we expand our U.S. footprint, and will help drive the initiatives of the strategy and business operations team.

You'll be responsible for building the systems that let us hire, develop, and retain great people as we continue our fast expansion. You'll work closely with the Talent Manager, Finance, Business Operations, and the broader executive leadership team, and act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and leadership team on people matters.

Key Responsibilities U.S. Employment Compliance Own state-by-state compliance as Maneva expands its U.S. employee base: tax registration, payroll setup, mandatory workplace posters, and required employee notices, all of which vary by state.

Build and maintain a repeatable process for evaluating new-state requirements as hiring expands, rather than handling each state reactively. Partner with Rippling, outside counsel, and Finance to ensure payroll, tax, and notice obligations are met on schedule for every state in which Maneva has employees.

Serve as Maneva 's go-to internal expert on U.S. state employment law as it applies to a distributed, remote-first workforce. Performance Management & Levelling Design and execute performance review cycles (6-month and annual) across the organization, tailored to company growth stage and business needs.

Own and maintain levelling frameworks across engineering (IC1–IC6) and non-technical roles; define competencies, expectations, and progression criteria, building on the framework already in place. Partner with department heads and the Talent Manager to calibrate performance data and inform talent decisions.

Design and facilitate manager training on feedback, goal-setting, and performance conversations. Maintain performance documentation and analytics to inform strategic people decisions. Compensation Administration Own day-to-day execution of compensation administration across all job levels and geographies; maintain salary bands.

Execute variable/commission plans for sales and other roles; ensure alignment with business goals. Execute ROE submissions, payroll adjustments, and comp/commission payouts, routing every payout through Finance for cost sign-off. Handle market increases, retention bonuses, and compensation requests with appropriate approvals.

Benefits & Wellness Administration Own benefits administration across the US and Canada. Coordinate benefits enrollment, education, and communication; manage plan changes. Administer COBRA coverage, health plan compliance, and employee welfare programs. Track and optimize benefits costs; provide leadership with regular reporting.

Contracts, Policies & Compliance Maintain and update U.S. and Canadian employment agreement templates. Own employee handbook and policy management for both Canada and the U.S.; refresh as laws and entities change. Manage people-related compliance: ROE submissions, payroll tax filings, and employment law compliance across all jurisdictions.

Maintain data integrity across HRIS systems; ensure clean records for auditing. Coordinate with external employment counsel as needed. Culture & Employee Engagement Partner with the Talent Manager on culture initiatives and engagement programs. Own recognition programs, including birthday and work-anniversary recognition.

Monitor and report on employee engagement signals; identify retention risks. Facilitate communication between leadership and employees. Systems, Automation & Operations Build automated workflows. Create dashboards and reporting for leadership on key HR metrics. Manage systems integration; ensure clean data flow between platforms.

Take ownership of ad-hoc projects and strategic initiatives. Business Operations Support Provide flexible support on cross-functional business initiatives as they arise — this portion of the role is intentionally variable rather than a fixed list of duties. Assist with insurance requirements and vendor/partnership coordination as needed.

Support with ad-hoc strategic initiatives such as fundraising and data room management, and partnership outreach. Support KPI and revenue schedule tracking in coordination with Finance Expect this allocation to flex up (e.g., during fundraising) and back down as business needs shift.

Requirements Required Experience 5+ years in people operations or HR, with experience scaling a company from roughly 50–300+ employees. Hands-on, current experience with U.S. state-level employment compliance — tax registration, payroll considerations, mandatory workplace posters, and employee notices — required.

Success leading people ops teams or managing complex, multi-jurisdiction workflows. Hands-on HRIS experience with Rippling; benefits administration. Track record designing performance cycles, levelling frameworks, and compensation structures. Based in Canada, ideally the Greater Toronto Area.

Core Competencies Deep, current knowledge of U.S. state employment law and how it varies by jurisdiction. Systems thinking and process design; ability to build scalable workflows. Strong stakeholder management across Finance, IT, Recruitment, and Leadership. Data-driven mindset; ability to turn HR data into clear recommendations.

Calm under pressure; ability to manage ambiguity, shifting priorities, and organizational change — including flexing between People Ops and BizOps work as needed. Attention to detail and compliance rigor. Clear communication; ability to explain HR and compliance concepts to non-experts.

Passion for building cultures where people feel valued and connected to mission. Technical Skills & Tools Proficiency with HRIS systems (Rippling preferred). Comfort building automation tools. Strong Excel and analytics skills. Nice to Have Experience in B2B SaaS, deep tech, or AI/manufacturing.

Familiarity with venture-backed, fast-growth company dynamics, including fundraise support. French language skills. Why Join Maneva Build an expanded people operations function from the ground up at a mission-driven AI company in a period of fast growth across Canada and the U.S.

You'll own the full employee lifecycle, lead Maneva 's U.S. compliance posture, and have direct influence on culture, talent strategy, and organizational effectiveness. Work closely with a collaborative leadership team.

You'll have autonomy to design systems, make strategic recommendations, and directly impact how Maneva attracts, develops, and retains world-class people — with occasional exposure to fundraising and broader business operations.

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

In this key role, you act as the operational backbone of our Munich office, driving efficiency, structure, and seamless daily execution. You will take full ownership of our workplace environment, fleet operations, vendor management, and internal administrative workflows as we continue to scale rapidly. Your proactive, hands-on approach directly ensures our team has the support and infrastructure needed to build the future of industrial robotics.

Drive Office Organization & Front Desk Management: Serve as the central point of contact for daily office operations, managing phone and mail communications, maintaining a representative environment, and coordinating cleaning teams and facility maintenance.
Automate & Lead Fleet Management: Oversee our entire vehicle fleet by managing leasing companies, vehicle acquisitions, and maintenance, while driving process automation using modern tools.
Manage Travel & Company Events: Plan and organize business trips, hotel bookings, and appointment scheduling, alongside organizing internal team gatherings, in-office events, and company-wide celebrations.
Office & Documentation Support: Serve as the on-site point of contact for invoice and documentation collection, checking cost centers, uploading physical invoices in our expense management system, plus occasional in-person support for signatures and NDAs.
Ensure Workplace Safety: Act as the designated safety officer, ensuring all health and safety regulations are strictly adhered to, monitored, and continuously optimized.
Coordinate External Vendors & Tradespeople: Actively manage third-party office service providers, building managers, and external suppliers to maintain smooth site operations.
Automate Operational Processes: Continuously evaluate internal administrative workflows, digitizing and streamlining manual tasks leveraging tools like Notion, Claude and Google Workspace.

s.h: We're looking for someone who has
s.t:
Completed vocational training or a degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Facility Management, Hospitality or comparable experience.
Several years of experience in Office Management or Workplace Operations.
Strong track record in process automation and documentation tools to digitize operations like fleet management.
High proficiency with tools like Notion, Moss, and Google Workspace.
Willingness to work onsite at our Munich office 4-5 days (up to) a week (with up to 1 Home Office day per week).
Culture-aligned mindset (e.g., "Strong ownership mindset", "Hands-on mindset", "Pragmatic working style").
Very good English skills and fluent German language skills (written and spoken) are required.

Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.
Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.
As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.
Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.
Wellpass membership (7,200+ studios across Germany), regular team events, and a team that takes both the work and the culture seriously
Flexible working hours, a modern office, and - depending on the role - the option to work from home.
Regular team events - from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.
About RobCo
Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that adapts to your use case, improves over time, and requires zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.
We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics.

With $160M raised from investors including Lightspeed, Lingotto Innovation, and Sequoia, 200+ people globally, and 2.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our RobCo Bay Area Demo Lab in San Francisco.

In this role, you will be the absolute engine of cross-divisional execution. You will collaborate daily with Product, Growth, Tech, Marketing, and Data teams to push critical business programs across the finish line.

You will map milestones, clear operational bottlenecks, run rigorous status checks, and ensure our studio moves with high velocity without fracturing into silos. You are a true "Program Pilot", someone who thrives under pressure, takes absolute ownership of project delivery, and ensures every cross-functional team has exactly what they need to win.
The entrepreneurial “get things done fast” is the most important criteria for Sunday. We are not looking for a traditional corporate administrator, building processes with long term effects or a high-level strategist who only builds slide decks. We are looking for an exceptionally hungry, agile operator to own end-to-end program and project management across our entire studio, who is focused on results.
This role is on fixed term - 1 year contract with the possibility of extension.

Own the Program & Project Lifecycle: Take immediate charge of tracking active cross-divisional programs, ensuring milestones are achieved on time and operational friction or project leakage is completely neutralized.
Enforce Cross-Functional Accountability: Act as the central node for project alignment. Conduct constant sprint and status check-ins with Game teams, UA managers, Data Scientists, and Developers. You are explicitly expected to have the difficult conversations required to resolve bottlenecks and challenge missing results.
Optimize Operational Handoffs: Standardize communication and workflows at critical project handoff points by ensuring all teams adhere strictly to formalized entry and exit criteria.
Drive Execution with an 80/20 ROI Focus: Evaluate project velocities against core business metrics (LTV, CPI, Spend, IAP, and absolute profit margin). Help teams maintain absolute focus on high-impact wins and flag low-value features drifting from our core roadmap.
Synthesize Leadership & Board Reporting: Transform complex project backlogs, program roadmaps, and cross-department timelines into crisp, data-backed status and blocker reports for senior executives and the board.

Agile Operator Mindset: You possess a profound generalist mindset. You are eager to master how multiple parts of our mobile entertainment value chain link together, translating program strategy directly into rapid execution.
Execution Grit: You operate with a lean, solution-driven mindset. You don't just manage by task lists; you manage by business outcomes. You own your time management and are accountable for delivery.
Transparent & Assertive Communicator: You practice direct, analytical, and respectful communication. You are completely unafraid to follow up cross-functionally for updates, expose alignment bottlenecks, or flag hidden project risks to leadership.
Project & Pipeline Specialist: You have exceptional logical tracking skills. You are highly proficient in using Jira, spreadsheets, and visual workflow tools to structure loose ideas into clean, scannable milestone roadmaps and program schedules.
Rapid Upskiller: You are an ambitious program professional looking to skip standard corporate ladders. You want to sit directly at the core of business operations, earning a masterclass in how a gaming studio scales by driving high-stakes commercial programs.

Build Your Skills, Not Just Your CV: At Sunday, you grow by doing. Real ownership, fast feedback, and steep learning curves are the norm. We don’t just offer development programs – we offer real problems to solve and the space to own them.

The Finance Operations Manager is responsible for overseeing payroll operations, banking and cash activities, VAT compliance coordination, and wider operational finance controls across the Group.
The role acts as the central coordination point between internal stakeholders and outsourced providers across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring the accurate, timely, and compliant delivery of payroll, payments, VAT, and regulatory processes.
This position combines strong operational finance capability with experience managing outsourced providers, international finance operations, and financial controls within a multi-entity environment.
The role focuses on the coordination, review, control, and operational oversight of outsourced and internally managed finance operations processes, rather than acting as the technical specialist responsible for preparing all underlying submissions directly.
The role currently has line management responsibility for the junior finance team members supporting accounts payable, payment processing, and VAT administration activities.
The finance function is also undergoing ongoing systems and process improvement initiatives to further strengthen operational efficiency, controls, and automation across the Group.

Technical Knowledge & Process Depth
The successful candidate will demonstrate a deep understanding of operational finance processes and the principles that underpin them. We are looking for someone who can clearly explain how processes work, why they exist, and how they connect to wider business objectives. The ability to break down complex processes, communicate them effectively to others, and support process improvement will be essential. In Practice you will be:
Able to build a P11D process from first principles
Able to articulate the end-to-end logic of a payroll run, identify where errors typically arise, and explain reconciliation steps to a junior colleague
Understands the VAT return process well enough to review submissions critically, not just pass information to advisors
Can walk through a payment run control framework and identify the risk points
Knows what KYC and international compliance documentation looks like and why it matters — not just where to file it
Essential Experience
Part-qualified or qualified (ACCA, CIMA, ACA or equivalent) with a strong operational finance background
Strong practical experience in payroll coordination, treasury management, and finance operations within a complex organisational structure.
Strong, demonstrable understanding of UK payroll processes and employment tax — including P11D, benefits-in-kind, pensions, and statutory payments
Proven experience working with outsourced payroll providers — managing the review and sign-off of their work
Practical experience overseeing banking platforms, payment controls, mandates and signatories
Direct experience coordinating VAT and compliance processes across multiple jurisdictions
Experience supervising or reviewing junior team members' work and communicating process logic clearly
Confident communicating with senior stakeholders, external providers, and international teams — written and verbal
Desirable
Experience within architecture, professional services, consultancy, or international project-based businesses
Exposure to international payroll operations and overseas banking — particularly China operations
Experience supporting finance systems improvements or automation initiatives
Familiarity with Sage 200, Deltek, or equivalent ERP/project systems
Language skills an advantage
Personal Attributes
We are a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and this role carries significant responsibility over sensitive financial data and processes. We are looking for someone who:
Is genuinely humble, willing to ask questions, acknowledge gaps, and learn the business
Is highly intelligent and intellectually curious — able to pick up new processes quickly and understand them deeply, not just operationally
Communicates with clarity and patience — able to explain complex processes simply to colleagues at all levels, including junior team members and non-finance stakeholders
Takes ownership without being asked — reliable, organised, and delivery-focused
Is calm, approachable and collaborative
Can be trusted with sensitive payroll, banking and compliance information — discretion is essential

The Opportunity 🚀
This role serves as the operational backbone of the Global Clinical Operations (GCO) team, developing a deep understanding of GCO's day-to-day workings in order to help operationalize its running.

You'll coordinate new projects, identify the right stakeholders, and partner closely with the GCO team, including GCO clinical leadership, to keep programs running smoothly. This is a hands-on operations role where success is measured by reliable execution, clean reporting, and strong cross-functional coordination.

You'll be the connective tissue between GCO sub-teams and partners across product, commercial, GTM, and customer success, giving you visibility into how clinical operations decisions ripple across the business.
What You’ll Own 💼

Serve as the operations point person across GCO sub-teams, keeping frameworks, timelines, and ways of working consistent.
Coordinate the GCO components of new projects end-to-end: identify stakeholders, track deliverables, and keep work moving across global clinical operations, product, and other partner teams.
Track spend against program budgets, flagging variances to leadership.
Spot and help close gaps or silos between GCO sub-teams by maintaining regular alignment touchpoints.
Build and maintain dashboards and reporting infrastructure that give leadership real-time visibility into program status, trends, and open decisions.
Pull together monthly operational updates, synthesizing data from Jira, Zendesk, Airtable, Salesforce, BI tools, and other program analytics into clear, actionable summaries.
Help connect operational metrics to clinical and business outcomes so leadership has a clear line of sight from day-to-day activity to impact.
Serve as a connector between GCO and commercial, GTM, and customer success teams, ensuring the right subject-matter expert is looped into RFPs, RFIs, and retention/expansion conversations.
Ensure feedback from client-facing teams is incorporated into GCO program planning and prioritization.
Identify opportunities to use AI tools, automation, and workflow improvements to save the team time and reduce manual work.
Support team members in getting up to speed on new tools and best practices as they're introduced.

What Success Looks Like 📈
In your first 12–18 months, you will have: Created and rolled out dashboards and reporting infrastructure that are adopted by GCO leadership.Improved operational efficiency across GCO, including reduced redundant meetings and streamlined recurring processes.Established a strong working rhythm with key GCO leadership and cross-functional partners.

Successfully managed multiple projects concurrently, hitting key milestones and deadlines, with consistent reporting/status updates so stakeholders always know where each project stands.

A Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, public health, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience in clinical/healthcare operations.
Demonstrated, hands-on experience in scheduling, budgets, and cross-functional coordination within clinical operations.
Strong program and process-design skills, shown through a program management certification or 2+ years of project management experience, including building/maintaining SOPs, governance documentation, and decision-informing reporting.
High comfort level with modern productivity and data tools (Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, Salesforce, Airtable, BI dashboards) and the ability to quickly learn new systems, including AI-enabled tools.
A demonstrated ability to operate across multiple fast-moving workstreams simultaneously without losing track of details.
Strong documentation skills, with the ability to create and maintain clear, reusable, well-organized documentation.
Extreme organization, with the ability to manage and maintain large databases and datasets accurately.
The ability to establish a process and cadence for audits, ensuring data and documentation stay accurate and current over time.

This role sits at the center of Carrot's Global Clinical Operations function, translating day-to-day execution into the reporting and coordination that leadership relies on to make decisions.

By keeping GCO's sub-teams aligned and connecting clinical operations to commercial and customer-facing teams, this person directly shapes how reliably Carrot delivers on its clinical programs — and how clearly that impact gets communicated across the business.

At Instructure , we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:
Foundry is a new division inside Instructure, built to generate new revenue with AI-built products. We operate as a portfolio of small pods, each charged with one product bet, under tight weekly governance. They operate independently, with dedicated resources, separate from the core business on purpose: different pace, different governance, and different rewards.
Our goal is to generate meaningful revenue within 12 to 18 months, so this isn’t an innovation lab. We’re building scaled businesses that customers pay for and retain well, and we’re measuring ourselves on revenue, not activity.
Instructure reaches roughly half of higher education in the United States, connecting a credential network of more than 13,000 institutions. Pair that distribution and data with a fast-moving team that builds leanly, and you have something no competitor has. That’s the opportunity New Markets exists to take.
How we work
A pod is two people: a Founder and a Builder, both hands on, close to the customer. The bet is deliberate: we invest in agent-developer tooling and tokens, not in headcount. An operating team of growth marketing, revenue operations, sales overlay, and G&A supports every pod, so founders stay on building products.
Every pod inherits an underlying platform with common design, development, and deployment harnesses, so no pod rebuilds the plumbing. Each pod runs through key phases with regular checkpoints where a governing board reviews progress or recommends a pivot or kill.
The rhythm is fast and transparent. Investor-style updates go out weekly. Demos and keep-or-kill checkpoints happen twice a month. Transparency is the operating model.

You’re the operational engine behind New Markets’ newest product bets. You’ll own the end-to-end go-to-market lifecycle for pod products, from market sizing and early strategy through launch, performance tracking, and the handoff when a product graduates into the core.

When a pod proves customers will pay, you make that motion repeatable and hand it to the full seller base. This is a blank-page job: the playbook doesn’t exist yet, and you’ll write it. The role reports directly to the President, New Markets, with a matrixed dotted line to Instructure’s Go-to-Market Strategy and Operations leadership.
What you’ll own
You own go-to-market operations across the portfolio, and you’re the voice of the New Markets business in the rooms where commercial decisions get made.

Own the end-to-end GTM lifecycle for pod products. Carry each product from market sizing and early strategy through launch planning, field execution, and post-launch performance tracking.
Shape the go-to-market approach with each pod. Partner with Pod Founders, marketing, and the sales overlay on ideal-customer definition, pricing and packaging input, channel strategy, and competitive positioning.
Design the sales motion. Build the coverage models, pipeline processes, forecasting cadences, and rules of engagement for the first seller cohort on each product.
Build the reporting backbone. Stand up and maintain the analytics in Salesforce and Excel that track pipeline health, win/loss, attach rates, average contract value, and renewal trends, and turn that data into insight leadership can act on.
Run launch readiness. Lead CRM buildout in Salesforce, playbook documentation, tool configuration, and alignment across enablement, marketing, finance, deal desk, and IT.
Own the graduation playbook. Define the criteria and the integration motion for products that complete a pod’s journey, so the full seller base can carry and sell the product without a messy handoff.
Be the voice of the business. Translate early-stage complexity into clear, data-backed narratives in planning forums, business reviews, and executive sessions, and support annual planning across capacity, quota, incentive design, and growth roadmaps.
What we expect
Blank page to operating framework. You go from nothing to a working system without a lot of hand-holding, then improve it as results and field feedback come in.
Rigor under ambiguity. You structure messy, early-stage go-to-market problems, build the analytical frame, and land a recommendation you can defend.
Accuracy you stand behind. The insights and reporting you put in front of leadership are right, and you own them.
Influence without authority. You move product, finance, marketing, and sales toward a shared plan without managing any of them.

Five or more years in sales operations, revenue operations, or a related go-to-market function.
Real experience supporting new-product launches or emerging-business initiatives, where the playbook didn’t exist yet.
Three or more years hands-on in Salesforce, building and maintaining reports, dashboards, and data structures.
Advanced Excel, comfortable building models, running variance analysis, and turning raw data into decision-ready output.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentations. A bachelor’s degree is preferred.
Your first 90 days
Month 1. Immerse yourself in the New Markets portfolio, the key stakeholders, and the current go-to-market infrastructure. Understand where each product sits in its lifecycle and find the most pressing operational gaps.
Month 3. Establish a clear view of performance across active pods: pipeline health, coverage, and leading indicators. Build or refine the reporting framework in Salesforce and Excel, and set a recurring operating rhythm with product and sales leadership.
Month 6. Own and drive the go-to-market motion for at least one pod through a checkpoint. Deliver an integration-readiness recommendation for any product approaching graduation, and present a prioritized roadmap for improving New Markets go-to-market operations to senior leadership.
This role isn’t for everyone

Base pay is market-competitive. You’ll be paid fairly against the market for the work, so you’re not taking a pay cut to be here. But the base is the floor, not the prize.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

We're after a Financial Operations Analyst to be the engine room of our day-to-day finance operations, covering customer accounts, supplier payments, and employee expenses. You'll be the go-to person the wider business turns to when they need something sorted, fast and right.
This is a cross-functional role by design. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer, People and teams right across Halter, not just Finance. If you like variety, own outcomes, and want your work to actually move the needle, this is for you.

Customers: Support accounts receivable process: invoicing, collections, and resolving billing queries quickly and professionally, protecting the customer relationship every step of the way.
Suppliers: Support our Financial Accountant on accounts payable: processing invoices, supplier onboarding, reconciling accounts, and being a reliable point of contact for our suppliers.
Employees: Manage the employee expense process: reviewing claims, reconciling corporate cards, employee reimbursements and keeping a high standard on details required without slowing the business down.
Cross-functional support: Be the first port of call for finance questions from teams across Halter: clear, fast, and helpful, every time.
Process improvement: Spot the gaps, fix the clunky stuff, and build better ways of working. We want someone who improves the system, not just runs it.
Month-end: Support close activities related to AR, AP and expenses, keeping our financial records accurate and audit-ready.

Experience in an accounts, finance operations, or accounts administration role, ideally across AP, AR or expenses. Sharp, numbers-hungry graduates who are keen to learn fast are welcome too.
Sharp attention to detail. You notice the things others miss, and you chase them down until they're resolved.
A genuine bias for action. You see a problem, you fix it. You don't wait to be told.
Comfortable operating at pace, with ambiguity, and without a playbook for everything.
Strong communication skills: confident chasing payments, questioning a number, or pushing back, whoever you're talking to.
A customer-first mindset, and pride in doing things properly, not just quickly.
Most of all: you're keen. You want to roll your sleeves up and build something exceptional, not just show up for the job title.

Real ownership from day one, with visibility across the whole business, not just Finance.
A seat on a team that's here to win, moves at max velocity, and backs each other to get there.
The chance to shape how finance operations work as Halter scales fast, across NZ, Australia and the US.
An office-first Auckland team that works hard, shares the wins, and doesn't take itself too seriously along the way.

Delicious snacks and drinks are available for your daily flow.
Healthy body, healthy mind. We're partnered with Southern Cross Health Insurance to support your well-being.
We offer 6 months of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks of fully paid secondary caregiver leave and many other parental benefits that support you and your family.
Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.
Our time to recharge is valued, we're offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.
Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.
Our Office First Approach
Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.
We're office first, not office only. Working from the office is our default, but we flex when needed. We have a high-trust culture where everyone is trusted to do what's best for Halter.
Our office vibe is special, the high energy and spectacular people make work enjoyable. Your growth and impact are unlimited here, coming from solving problems, innovating, and constantly learning from each other.
Join our team
Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement.

If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!
If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!
Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram .

s.h: Why our team loves working at Halter
s.t:
Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.
Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.
You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our $1,000 personal growth fund.

Why Harvey
At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.
Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.
At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

We’re looking for a senior operator to own the quality bar behind Harvey’s human evaluations. As we scale globally, the volume of eval work is growing 10x, but volume only matters if the output is trusted. This role makes Human Data’s signal decision-grade: rigorous, calibrated, and reproducible enough that Product, Engineering, and AI Research act on it to ship.
As a member of our Evaluation Operations team, you’ll work alongside our Evaluation Operations Manager (who runs throughput and coordination) and partner closely with Applied Legal Researchers, Product, Engineering, and AI Research. You'll set the standard for what "good" looks like across eval data and methodology, and own the data analyses to make conclusions that teams will rely on, building the stakeholder trust that lets EPD act on the signal.

Own the quality bar for Harvey’s human evaluations: define what “good” looks like for eval methodology and data analysis, and produce decision-grade outputs for EPD
Author and maintain the evaluation guidelines, instructions, and databases that contract attorneys work from
Standardize and streamline rubric and evaluation design into repeatable templates and one documented methodology, partnering with Applied Legal Research (ALR), who supplies feature-specific legal depth
Own contract-attorney quality: onboarding, calibration training, inter-rater reliability, and the feedback loop (including benchmarks and gold references) that keeps judgment consistent across attorneys and over time
Conducting quantitative and qualitative statistical analyses, diagnosing error states, investigating root causes, and turning raw eval results into a structured, prioritized signal Product and ALR can act on
Run QA on vendor and contract-attorney deliverables against a defined bar before results inform a launch decision
Ensure the quality bar holds across jurisdictions and non-English geographies as coverage expands
Establish one standard, documented way to analyze eval results, and build lightweight operational dashboards to track rater capability and eval-program health
Support ALR in a review step that certifies an evaluation is sound before it scales to contract attorneys
Partner with ALR and Analytics to determine where human eval aligns with online signal and where it can provide expanded insights
What You Have
6+ years in product operations, research operations, evaluation/QA operations, or quality program management
A track record of owning quality inputs (guidelines, instructions, benchmarks, QA procedures) for complex, expert-driven or human-in-the-loop work
Experience onboarding, training, and calibrating a distributed pool of expert raters, annotators, or reviewers, and running the feedback loop that improves their quality over time
Enough grounding in measurement concepts (calibration, inter-rater reliability, sampling, rubric design) to independently set up and own the quality of our evaluation loop yourself
Experience with running quantitative and qualitative data analyses, interpreting and running statistical tests on evaluation data (natively or with AI tool support), and communicating conclusions to various stakeholders
A record of scaling and streamlining evaluation quality processes under shipping pressure, with a bias toward documentation and reproducibility over one-off analysis
Ability to work deeply with domain experts (e.g., ALR / lawyers) and translate nuanced judgment into repeatable, documented standards
Strong cross-functional coordination across Product, Engineering, Research, ALR, and data providers/vendors
Clear communicator who can build credibility and trust with stakeholders
Bias to action and high ownership, from writing the guideline to auditing a vendor batch line by line

Experience in legal tech or working with domain experts in regulated industries
Experience owning quality across multiple markets, languages, or jurisdictions
Built calibration, inter-rater reliability, or capability-tracking systems for annotation or evaluation pipelines
Experience transitioning evaluation work in-house or otherwise improving evaluation ROI
Familiarity with LLM-as-judge / automated evaluation used alongside human eval
Early employee at a hyper-growth startup, or experience at a world-class product or platform operations org

The Partner Enablement Operations Manager is a senior operator and builder responsible for designing and running a scalable, predictable, and data-driven operating model for partner enablement at Databricks.
This role serves as the operational backbone and strategic integrator for partner enablement, connecting global strategy to the execution across AMER, EMEA, and APJ regions while ensuring programs are delivered consistently, efficiently, and at scale.
The ideal candidate brings strong executive presence, systems thinking, and a bias for automation. They know how to reduce operational friction, build governance that scales, and introduce AI-enabled workflows that improve responsiveness without adding unnecessary complexity or headcount.
We are looking for a builder who can architect operating systems and drive scalability and excellence for the future.

Own the partner enablement operating model, including core planning cadences, governance mechanisms, and execution frameworks that connect strategy to execution.
Run QBRs, MBRs, and executive reviews for partner enablement leadership, using clear metrics and forward-looking insights to drive accountability and decision-making.
Lead end-to-end execution of partner enablement initiatives, ensuring timelines, dependencies, and deliverables are managed effectively across functions and regions.
Build and maintain dashboards and operating reviews that surface partner engagement, program performance, risk signals, and areas requiring intervention.
Act as a key point of contact for cross-regional operational issues and escalations, resolving immediate friction while converting recurring issues into structural improvements.
Design and implement scalable workflows, SOPs, SLAs, and intake mechanisms that improve consistency, reduce manual effort, and create a better experience for internal stakeholders and partners.
Introduce AI-enabled and automation-first workflows for intake, reporting, support, certification, and partner operations where they can safely improve speed, quality, and scale.
Collaborate closely with the Partner organization, Learning and Enablement, Professional Services, and other cross-functional teams to remove friction and improve execution across the partner ecosystem.
Partner closely with the broader operations business to drive cross-functional leverage of ideas and excellence, ensuring new methods and operational innovations are scaled beyond just partner operations.
Establish clear ownership models, decision rights, and governance guardrails to support regional nuance without creating shadow processes or operational inconsistencies.

10+ years of experience in Learning Operations, Program Management, Professional Services Operations, or a related operational leadership field in a high-growth technology environment.
Proven experience supporting global or multi-region teams and translating central strategy into executable operating plans.
Preferred experience in the Data & AI space, with a strong understanding of Databricks' platform capabilities, key differentiators, and end-to-end solutions, and the ability to work effectively with technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated ownership of operating cadence, forecasting, planning, and execution frameworks in a complex, matrixed environment.
Strong analytical capability and the ability to turn data into executive insight, operational decisions, and measurable business outcomes.
Experience improving processes and workflows, with a clear track record of reducing manual effort and increasing scale through automation or AI-enabled solutions.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions without direct authority.
Ability to work independently, manage priorities across time zones, and drive execution in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
Must be open to working a flexible schedule, including frequent late hours to accommodate discussions with the broader enablement team and partner liaisons, the majority of whom are based in the AMER timezone.

Experience in partner enablement, customer education, learning operations, or training operations.
Deep expertise working with and for System Integrators (SIs) and ISVs, with a strong grasp of their core operational principles and business models.
Fluency with AI tools, workflow automation, and analytics platforms used to streamline operations and generate actionable insights.
Strong commercial and operational acumen, including comfort with utilization, forecasting, partner spend, margin thinking, or RevOps-aligned execution.
Experience operating in a highly matrixed international environment with sensitivity to regional and cultural nuance.

You will play a central role in shaping how partner enablement scales at Databricks.
This is a high-visibility role with meaningful impact, offering the opportunity to build a more efficient, governed, and AI-enabled operating model that helps our partner ecosystem grow with the business.
If you enjoy turning ambiguity into structure, building systems that remove friction, and helping teams scale through better operations rather than more manual work, this role is for you.
Success Metrics
Operational Predictability: Build a disciplined partner enablement operating cadence where risks are surfaced early and execution is measurable and consistent.
Stakeholder Experience and Self-Sufficiency: Increase the percentage of standard partner enablement requests handled through structured, low-touch, or self-service workflows.
Escalation Management and Process Resilience: Reduce recurring operational friction by improving escalation handling, clarifying ownership, and improving systemic resolution of recurring issues.
Scalable Execution: Improve throughput, consistency, and delivery quality across global partner enablement programs without relying on incremental manual work.
AI-Enabled Transformation: Deploy practical AI-enabled workflows that improve speed, visibility, and efficiency across intake, reporting, support, and partner operations.
About Databricks
Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents.

Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn , X , YouTube , and Instagram .

At Databricks, we strive to provide comprehensive benefits and perks that meet the needs of all of our employees. For specific details on the benefits offered in your region click here .
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
At Databricks, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can excel. We take great care to ensure that our hiring practices are inclusive and meet equal employment opportunity standards.

Individuals looking for employment at Databricks are considered without regard to age, color, disability, ethnicity, family or marital status, gender identity or expression, language, national origin, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, veteran status, and other protected characteristics.

s.h: About the role: What's in the Box
s.t:
Based in Auckland and reporting to the ANZ CEO, the General Manager for New Zealand leads the overall performance, growth and strategic direction of HelloFresh New Zealand; one of the HelloFresh’s most established and innovative markets.

Owning the New Zealand P&L end-to-end, you set the strategy to maximize sustainable growth and profitability, sharpen the local proposition, and represent HelloFresh with government, regulators, partners and the wider community.

You deliver through influence, aligning matrixed teams across growth, product, marketing, finance, customer care and operations behind a shared plan.
Above all, you will change the way Kiwis eat, forever!

Own the P&L: Take full accountability for HelloFresh New Zealand’s commercial and financial performance, leading annual planning, forecasting and business reviews with ANZ and Global leadership.
Set the strategy: Define and execute the roadmap that returns the market to sustainable growth and profitability across customer acquisition, retention, pricing and margin.
Sharpen the proposition: Partner with Global teams to pilot new products and propositions, and strengthen the local relevance of HelloFresh for Kiwi customers.
Lead through influence: Align and energise matrixed teams across growth, product, marketing, finance, customer care and operations to reach shared business objectives without direct line authority.
Represent the business: Act as the senior spokesperson for HelloFresh New Zealand with government, regulators, industry bodies and strategic partners.
Shape Group strategy: Feed insight, innovation and learnings from New Zealand back into regional and Global decision-making.

P&L leadership: A track record of owning a P&L or a major commercial function, ideally blending top-tier consulting, high-growth startup or comparable fast-paced experience.
Commercial and product instinct: Strong grounding in D2C marketing and product development, with the judgement to turn strategy into measurable growth.
Influence without authority: The ability to set clear direction and bring senior, matrixed stakeholders along through collaboration rather than formal reporting lines.
Data-driven mindset: A highly analytical approach, comfortable using data to prioritise and to hold the business to its plan.
Local market understanding: Familiarity with the New Zealand market and consumer, or a real ability to build local relevance and credibility quickly.
Drive and food enthusiasm: Entrepreneurial energy, resilience and a genuine enthusiasm for good food and the HelloFresh mission.

Compensation with upside: A highly attractive package with significant equity upside for a senior leader in a leading global food-technology company.
Own a market: The rare chance to lead an entire market and shape its direction end to end.
Hybrid working: Three days in the Auckland office and two days working from home each week.
Work from anywhere: Up to three weeks working from a location of your choice in any 12-month period.
Wellbeing support: Free Headspace access (extendable to five friends or family) and a confidential Employee Assistance Program.
Learning and growth: HelloFresh Academy sessions, a function-led L&D budget and a structured mentoring program.
Time to recharge: Additional HF Days that grow with tenure, plus sabbatical leave for longer-serving team members.
HelloFresh discount: 70% off your HelloFresh boxes, plus friends-and-family discounts.
Are you the missing ingredient? If this sounds like a tasty opportunity, we’d be excited to hear from you. We aim to review your profile and respond within 5 business days.

We're transforming the grocery industry
At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community.

We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.
Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
Instacart is a Flex First team
There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.
Why this role is on the menu
Eversight, part of Instacart, is building next-generation data insights and analytics platforms that help leading CPGs & Retailers make smarter, faster decisions across pricing, promotions, retail media, and omni-commerce.

We're hiring a Senior Revenue Operations Manager to build and run end-to-end revenue operations across our Commercial organization (Sales and Customer Success), spanning both CPG and Retail.

This is a build-and-own role, not a request-response one: you'll identify what the business needs before it's escalated to you, bring a recommendation, and drive it to completion.

You'll report directly to the Director of Sales Capabilities & Strategy, with broad latitude to design process, own reporting, and act as a trusted partner to commercial leadership across Eversight Sales, Customer Success, and Product, along with cross functional partners like Strategic Finance, Commercial Partnerships and Brand Partnerships.
What you'll cook up in your first year
Standardized reporting and forecasting models live across CPG and Retail, giving commercial leadership one clear view of pipeline, renewals, and customer health
Dashboards built and adopted across Sales and Customer Success that leadership actually uses to make decisions, tracking pipeline, renewal rate, expansion, and churn risk
Operational gaps identified and fixed before anyone had to ask, each tied to a measurable improvement in forecast accuracy, data integrity, or process efficiency
AI tools, agents, and workflow automations built and shipped that eliminate recurring reporting and data cleanup work, cutting manual operational overhead across the commercial org
Trusted operational relationships built across every team you touch, with clean handoffs and no surprises
Process documentation and standardized frameworks built as you go, not bolted on after the fact

Bachelor's degree in Business, Analytics, Statistics, or related field
7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or a similar function within a SaaS company; experience in CPG, Retail, or trade promotion/pricing analytics highly preferred
Proven ability to analyze and interpret complex data sets to deliver actionable insight
Fluent in using AI tools, agents, and workflow automations to eliminate manual reporting and data cleanup, as a core part of how you operate rather than an occasional add-on
Experience with SQL and Tableau
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present findings to leadership
Demonstrated ability to identify challenges, prioritize solutions, and execute improvements independently
Adept at working cross-functionally with a focus on aligning multiple stakeholders toward shared goals
A self-starter able to operate independently in a fast-paced environment

MBA
Working knowledge of Salesforce and Planhat (or comparable CS platform)
Understanding of the CPG trade promotion, pricing, and revenue growth management landscape
Understanding of the Retail Merchandising landscape

Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Website Operations Manager to join our Marketing team.
Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family.

This role will deliver value from our online properties, including the operational, technical, and strategic aspects, ensuring it meets business needs, supports marketing and compliance goals, and identifies and champions growth opportunities across the organization.
You will report into the Associate Director, Marketing, Websites & Digital Reputation.

This position is based in our New York City office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid
The base pay for this role is: $106,812.00 - $140,190.75 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program and annual performance bonuses.

Manage Oscar’s Content Management System (CMS) and ensure it is optimized for internal use, including content updates, landing page creation, and form functionality.
Maintain and optimize existing pages, identifying and implementing opportunities for new content and improved user experience.
Train internal teams (e.g., Compliance, Pharmacy) on best practices and self-service content updates.
Ensure accurate set up of Google Analytics to monitor website performance, user behavior, and key metrics, reporting insights and opportunities to stakeholders.
Drive and manage A/B testing strategies and collaborate with internal teams to identify and implement optimization opportunities.
Ensure the company’s digital presence is protected and aligned with business goals.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align website goals with broader business objectives.
Develop and execute a comprehensive SEO strategy to improve organic search rankings, staying ahead of AI-driven changes in search results and adapting strategies accordingly.
Compliance with app applicable laws and regulations.

Bachelors Degree or 4+ years commensurate experience.
4+ years of experience in website management, digital marketing, or a related field.
3+ years managing and executing in CMS platforms (e.g., Contentful, WordPress), Google Analytics, and SEO tools. 2+ years A/B or multivariate testing experience (test and target or other vendors).

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.
At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
Our Recruiting Team plays a vital role in shaping exceptional teams at Roblox and driving our future growth.

At the center of the recruiting experience is our Recruiting Coordination team, who handle everything from scheduling interviews, tracking candidate data and helping improve internal processes all while ensuring a positive experience for all candidates.

We are looking for a motivated Recruiting Coordinator to join our team and contribute to the next stage of Roblox's success! This position is a six-month short-term employment with the opportunity to be considered for extension and/or full-time employment pending performance and business needs.

This is a hybrid position based in our San Mateo, CA offices.
You Will
Partner with members of our recruiting and hiring teams to create a phenomenal candidate experience
Manage the candidate interview process including scheduling a high-volume of interviews and being the contact for day-of questions
Greeting, hosting, and managing the experience for candidates visiting the office for in-person interviews
Oversee and facilitate a seamless candidate onsite experience, ensuring a positive welcome for all visitors.
Manage high-complexity operational workflows, including job approvals, Talent Review coordination, offer letter generation, and interview scheduling, ensuring data accuracy and compliance while maintaining exceptional stakeholder relationships and a white-glove candidate experience.
Maintain adherence to established SLAs and actively monitor time-to-schedule, time-to-approve and ticket resolution metrics, ensuring high velocity and operational integrity.
Proactively own and solve the root cause of scheduling and operational challenges or inconsistencies

2+ years of experience with a proven history of managing high-volume, complex operational tasks. Experience with Greenhouse and the recruiting space is preferred.
Exceptional Attention to Detail: Proven ability to reliably manage operational tasks with accuracy in high-stakes, complex and in some cases, confidential environments
Strong Stakeholder Partnership & Communication: Demonstrated ability to frame communication around stakeholder needs, influence outcomes, and communicate with impact and empathy.
A Strategic Mindset: Demonstrated systems thinking and experience designing processes/guardrails to solve problems at scale.
High-Volume/High-Velocity Execution: Ability to manage a high volume of requests, prioritize rapid response times, and handle scheduling requests with precision and speed.

A Curious Problem Solver: Demonstrated ability to perform initial research and diagnosis of issues, consolidating questions and proposing pre-vetted options or solutions back to stakeholders, TA and hiring teams when requests are incomplete or unclear.
Data-Fluent: Able to use and translate data into actionable solutions when partnering with others.
Proactive and Accountable: Own the outcome of your processes and routinely propose pre-vetted options and Plan Bs instead of just reporting a problem.
Timely and Professional Communicator: Ensure all candidate communication is professional, timely, and detail-oriented, reflecting a white-glove candidate experience.
Committed to Service Delivery: View your service as the foundation of trust for candidates and stakeholders, recognizing that dependability is the team's currency.

Atuar nos processos de Identificação e Formalização (ID&F) com foco na análise de fraude documental, cadastral e de identidade, garantindo que clientes e operações estejam corretamente identificados e em conformidade com políticas internas, normas regulatórias e padrões de prevenção a riscos e fraudes.
Responsabilidades e Atribuições
