## Your Purpose ##
We are pleased to be hiring for an Environmental Operations Manager to join our growing Enviromental department. In this role you will manage all operational environmental activities of MSC Cruises fleet of cruise vessels ensuring operational excellence and adherence to all applicable environmental rules and regulations and Company Policy.

* Plans and manages logistics and waste disposal activities, ensuring the full compliance with all applicable regulations and Company policies;
* Monitors vessels- activities daily in order to ensure their compliance with all applicable environmental regulations and company policies. Drives operational fleet activities through daily communication with the ship commands and onboard officers;
* Participates in audit inspections, and ISO 14001 and 21070 certifications as required.
* Manages the administrative and operational environmental activities with Port Agencies and stakeholders, developing strategies and programs;
* Analyses budget and disbursement accounts for managed vessels and provides input to Head of Fleet Environmental Operations.
* Coordinates shipside activities, ensuring appropriate documentation, related to CLIA, Port Authorities and other stakeholders;
* Deals with environmental services vendors and Agencies in order to ensure the ships- environmental compliance, negotiating costs/rebates and provides support for any relevant financial matters;
* Reviews and ensures the correct application of procedures, Manuals, Record Books, and all applicable environmental related documentation;
* Researches, follows and updates environmental legislation, and national and international rules regarding all environmental matters;
* Administers all reporting schemes (ESI, EPI, MRV, IMO DCS, Ocean Guardian etc) for managed vessels and reports results to Head of Fleet Environmental Operations.
* Analyses new business opportunities in order to optimize the full waste management and water supply process for the fleet, including the new building projects. Analyses costs and environmental performances and cooperates with Port Operations in the development of programs in the environmental related area;
* Cooperates in all Environmental Department projects and with all multidisciplinary projects involving different MSC Cruises Departments.
* Participates and assist with the fleet training program and managed vessels as required by the Head of Environmental Systems Training & Audit.
* Assists with the administration of the overall environmental program at Ocean Cay, including but not limited to waste management, training, compliance, audit, and reporting.
* Performs other relevant tasks as required by operational departmental needs.
## Your Journey so far ##
· Fluent in oral and written English. Knowledge of Italian and other major European languages is an advantage.
· Environmental science university studies preferred. Post-graduate specific studies in the area of interest preferred.
· A wide knowledge of the Cruise/Maritime industry (preferred).
· Experience onboard cruise ships as either Environmental Officer for a minimum of three years (preferred), or
Deck Officer / Engineer Officer with at least two years of professional experience in ashore environmental
related roles.
· Some of the above requirements can also be fulfilled by having three years plus of working experience in
environmental-related sector.
· Ability to use Microsoft Office and other company specific operating platforms and databases.
· Able to manage communication at all levels. Proven ability to lead and contribute to a harmonious and
productive team environment.
· Ability to understand and interpret various complex regulations and environmental matters.
· Ability to understand and interpret various financial matters affecting the Department.
· Ability to work in a multicultural and international working environment.
· Ability to perform under pressure.
## Your Essentials ##
* Fluent in oral and written English. Knowledge of Italian and other major European languages is an advantage;
* The existing right to live and work in the EU is required

## Your Purpose ##
The Technical Manager Islands Operations provides strategic technical leadership and oversight for all engineering operations at Ocean Cay Msc Marine Reserve and Sandy Cay. The role ensures support to the Site Chief Engineer that effectively manages daily engineering operations while maintaining the highest standards of safety, reliability, compliance, asset performance, and operational efficiency.
The Technical Manager oversees major engineering projects, capital investments, preventive maintenance strategies, technical budgets, contractor management, and engineering performance. The position supports the Site Chief Engineer by providing technical direction, mentoring, and governance while ensuring compliance with MSC corporate standards and international regulations

* Provide strategic technical leadership and oversight of all engineering operations on Ocean Cay.
* Directly supervise, mentor, and evaluate the performance of the Site Chief Engineer.
* Review and approve maintenance strategies, preventive maintenance programs, and asset management plans.
* Oversee the operation and reliability of power generation, water production, wastewater treatment, HVAC, electrical distribution, IT infrastructure, marine assets, buildings, and support facilities.
* Approve engineering budgets, CAPEX projects, procurement plans, and major technical expenditures.
* Lead major engineering projects from planning through commissioning.
* Ensure engineering systems comply with MSC standards, Bahamian regulations, and international codes.
* Review engineering reports, maintenance KPIs, equipment reliability, and operational performance.
* Lead root cause analysis (RCA) for major equipment failures and implement reliability improvement initiatives.
* Develop long-term asset replacement and lifecycle management strategies.
* Promote continuous improvement, innovation, and energy efficiency initiatives.
* Support emergency response and provide technical leadership during critical operational events.
* Develop succession plans and oversee technical training for engineering management and supervisory staff.
## Your Journey so far ##
* Experience managing power generation, water production, wastewater treatment, HVAC, electrical distribution, IT infrastructure, and marine assets.
* Ability to effectively plan, organize, delegate and control the work process, and to communicate effectively with senior management, contractors, and multidisciplinary engineering teams.
## Your Essentials ##
* Minimum of 5 years in a senior engineering leadership or management position
* Fluent in spoken and written English, excellent verbal and written communication skills. Knowledge of an additional language is an advantage.
* Strong technical report writing and presentation skills.

We are committed to building a future that values diverse perspectives, embraces the world beyond borders, and fosters an inclusive environment where every individual feels valued, respected and empowered to be their authentic selves. Our commitment extends to taking meaningful, measurable actions that have a long-term positive impact on our guests, our employees and our planet.

The Campaign Operations team sits at the heart of Carwow’s OEM and Media business. We turn ambitious commercial ideas into high-quality digital advertising campaigns that deliver strong results for our clients and meaningful revenue for Carwow.
We work closely with Sales, Product, Data, Marketing, Engineering and external partners to deliver campaigns across Carwow’s automotive media portfolio. Our mission is to make campaign delivery accurate, efficient and scalable while continuously improving how we work through better processes, technology and innovation.

As Campaign Operations Manager, your mission will be to own the successful delivery and optimisation of digital advertising campaigns from initial planning through to post-campaign analysis.
You’ll ensure campaigns launch accurately, deliver against their objectives and provide an excellent experience for our clients and internal teams. You’ll proactively solve delivery challenges, identify opportunities to maximise revenue and use data to turn campaign performance into valuable insights.
Success in this role means consistently delivering high-quality campaigns while helping Campaign Operations become smarter, more efficient and increasingly scalable.

Own the end-to-end delivery of digital advertising campaigns, from planning and setup through to optimisation, reporting and post-campaign analysis.
Ensure campaigns are implemented accurately, launched on time and delivered in line with agreed objectives.
Monitor campaign performance and proactively optimise activity to improve delivery and results.
Troubleshoot campaign issues, resolve blockers and minimise delivery and revenue risk.
Produce high-quality campaign reports and post-campaign analysis decks that translate performance data into clear, actionable insights.
Present campaign performance, findings and recommendations to internal stakeholders and external clients when required.
Build strong working relationships with Sales, Product, Data, Marketing, Engineering and external partners.
Identify commercial opportunities, including campaign upweights, extensions and improvements that could deliver additional value for clients and Carwow.
Continuously review Campaign Operations processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy and scalability.
Support the adoption of automation, AI and new technology across Campaign Operations while maintaining strong quality-control standards.

Experience managing and delivering digital advertising campaigns within a publisher, media owner, agency or ad-tech environment.
Strong understanding of digital advertising operations, campaign setup, optimisation, delivery and reporting.
Experience using an ad server or campaign management platform, ideally Google Ad Manager.
Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, stakeholders and deadlines at the same time.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn campaign data into clear insights and recommendations.
A proactive approach to identifying risks, resolving problems and improving campaign performance.
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to delivering accurate, high-quality work.
Confident communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to explain campaign performance clearly.
A commercially minded approach, with an understanding of how effective campaign management supports revenue and client retention.
A collaborative, adaptable mindset and an interest in improving processes through technology, automation and AI.

Experience working within the automotive, publishing or digital media industry.
Knowledge of programmatic advertising, paid social, YouTube or off-site display campaigns.
Experience with demand-generation or lead-generation campaigns.
Familiarity with platforms such as DV360, Meta Ads Manager, Salesforce, Driftrock or audience-management platforms.
Previous involvement in process-improvement, automation or AI projects.

## Your Purpose ##
The Regional Security Operational Manager - Private Destinations is responsible for leading the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of security operations across the company's designated private destinations. The role focuses primarily on operational development projects, security infrastructure planning, risk management programs, and the establishment of security standards that support the safe and secure operation of private destination assets.
Acting as a regional representative of the Global Security Department, the Regional Security Operational Manager provides strategic guidance and operational oversight for all security-related initiatives associated with private destinations, ensuring the protection of guests, crew members, employees, contractors, facilities, and company assets.
The position serves as the primary liaison between private destination operations and the Global Security Department, ensuring the consistent implementation of corporate security policies, procedures, standards, and risk management practices across all assigned locations. The role is responsible for driving security project development, enhancing operational readiness, and supporting the delivery of long-term security objectives for private destinations.
In addition to its primary focus on private destination security operations and development projects, the position will provide operational support to Fleet Security activities when required by the Global Security Department, ensuring alignment with broader corporate security strategies and operational priorities.

*Private Destination Security (Ocean Cay & Sandy Cay):*
* Act as the regional representative of the Global Security Department for the USA, Caribbean, and private destinations.
* Provide timely security advice and support to regional leadership, vessel management teams, and business stakeholders.
* Maintain awareness of regional threats, geopolitical developments, criminal activity, and operational risks that may impact business operations.
* Act as the regional security lead during crisis, incident response, and business continuity events, coordinating with Global Security,
* Oversee all daily security operations at Ocean Cay and Sandy Cay private destinations.
* Oversee regional security service providers and contracted security personnel.
* Ensure that the Global standard procedures are implemented to safeguard guests, staff, facilities, infrastructure, and company assets.
* Promote a strong security culture and compliance with company security expectations.
* Conduct regular security assessments and Internal audits of private destination operations.
* Oversee security team development, recruitment, performance management, training programmes, and certification requirements.
* Develop and deliver security awareness and compliance training for security personnel and island-based staff.
* Coordinate emergency preparedness, drills and crisis management activities.
* Oversee security systems including CCTV, access control, alarms, perimeter protection, and monitoring solutions.
* On behalf of Global Security, oversee and support security projects and technology enhancements.
* Produce executive monthly reports of incidents, lessons learned, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
* Support the Regional Security investigator when required to investigate security incidents at private destinations.
* Build and maintain effective relationships with the relevant Maritime Authorities.
*Fleet Security Oversight (when required):*
* Oversee security operations for vessels trading within U.S. and Caribbean waters and ports.
* Guide compliance with applicable maritime security regulations and company standards.
* Support vessel security assessments, audits, inspections, and security reviews.
* Produce executive reports, lessons learned, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
* When required, oversee all security operations at MSC Cruise Terminal AA and other Terminals within the USA (when the MSC Vessel is alongside)
## Your Journey so far ##
* Fluent in English (written and spoken).
* Full understanding and practical application of the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.
* Previous experience as a Chief Security Officer aboard a major international cruise line is highly desirable and considered a significant advantage.
* Experience working with law enforcement, government agencies, port authorities, and international security stakeholders is highly desirable.
* Certified Port Facility Security Officer (PFSO) and Ship Security Officer (SSO).
* Minimum of 8-10 years' experience in corporate security, maritime security, or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience managing security operations within the maritime, cruise, or transportation industries.
* Thorough knowledge of cruise industry operations and awareness of comparable security practices across competing organizations.
* Strong understanding of maritime security frameworks, regulations, and industry best practices.
* Above-average ability to manage crises, resolve problems, and handle sensitive situations with tact, diplomacy, and professionalism.
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, written communication, and negotiation skills.
* Proven ability to build and maintain productive working relationships within a diverse and collaborative team environment.
* High level of integrity, discretion, sound judgment, and professionalism.
* Ability to develop, review, and maintain security procedures, reports, policies, and operational manuals.
* Proven capability to assess risks, investigate incidents, and implement effective mitigation measures.
* Must have the legal right to live and work in the United States.
* Ability to travel internationally without restriction and establish effective local stakeholder networks within the assigned area of responsibility.
* Willingness to undertake regular visits to vessels, ports, terminals, and private destinations.
* Ability to respond to security incidents and emergencies at short notice.
* Availability outside normal business hours when operationally required to support operational and emergency needs.

· Act as the operational right hand to the RVP, collaborating on forecasting, performance analysis, GTM planning, pipeline management, and regional execution.

Experience guiding and coaching remote analysts or offshore resources to support core business functions, ensuring alignment, clarity, and impact.
A growth mindset, you embrace change, seek feedback, and aren’t afraid to roll up your sleeves and drive results.

About Neon
Neon is a global payments and e-commerce platform designed to help game publishers earn more money and independence from app stores. We believe commerce should be open and transparent: clear decisions, actionable insights, and aligned incentives.

Founded by payments, fintech and gaming veterans, Neon focuses on product and partnership excellence: we share the playbook, co-pilot decisions, and abstract away risk and complexity for our customers. We’re replacing old-school, black-box relics with clear, modern, and developer-centric infrastructure.
As an early team member, you’ll have the opportunity to shape and scale Neon’s product and culture, making a direct impact on our growth and success. You’ll join a collaborative, diverse team from world-class companies like Apple, Affirm, Unity, and Visa, backed by renowned VC's including Thrive, a16z, Griffin Gaming, Ribbit, and Renegade. If you want to build disruptive technology, challenge the status quo, and help game creators thrive on their own terms, read on.

Neon is a gaming-focused Merchant of Record platform serving game publishers globally. We process payments across 50+ markets through multiple PSPs simultaneously, operating as the seller of record across card networks, local wallets, A2A rails, and alternative payment methods.
This role owns the operational backbone of that system: dispute and chargeback management, fraud operations, compliance monitoring, payment performance tracking, and operational support for Customer Success.

As the senior operator across these functions, the Payment Operations Manager sets operational standards, defines targets, owns PSP and partner operational relationships, and is accountable for outcomes across payments, risk, fraud, and compliance.

The role partners with the Head of Payments and the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader as a peer across all four functions.
This is a senior individual-contributor role . The Manager title reflects the seniority and ownership scope of the role and function, not direct reports at this stage.

Dispute & Chargeback Operations
Own dispute intake, evidence compilation, and resolution across all active payment processors and markets.
Define and own resolution SLAs and win-rate targets; identify systemic patterns and drive fixes with product and risk leads.
Prioritize and drive the roadmap for internal dispute tooling as operational infrastructure matures.
Fraud Operations
Own fraud operations and oversee investigations and transaction reviews in partnership with the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader.
Set monitoring and escalation standards across screening and decisioning tools; maintain case integrity and decision quality.
Track fraud loss trends across markets and game titles; surface and act on emerging attack patterns before they scale.
Payment Performance Monitoring
Own tracking of authorization rates, payment success rates, decline codes, and fraud losses across processors and markets.
Own post-launch metric reviews for new payment methods against defined performance thresholds.
Define the operational dashboard and alerting standard; ensure anomalies are caught before they become publisher-impacting incidents.
Customer Success Support
Serve as the senior operational point of contact for payment-related requests escalated by Customer Success.
Lead deep dives into publisher payment performance, dispute trends, and fraud exposure, producing structured analysis CS can use directly in publisher conversations.
Own the operational response to payment incidents: root cause investigation, timeline reconstruction, and remediation communication.
PSP & Partner Management
Own day-to-day operational relationships with PSPs and payment partners, including performance reviews, escalations, and issue resolution.
Hold partners accountable to performance and SLA commitments; drive improvement where markets or methods underperform.
Process, Tooling & Standards
Set and maintain operational standards, runbooks, and process documentation that others follow.
Prioritize automation opportunities and partner with the Head of Payments, Risk & Compliance, and engineering to translate operational gaps into product and tooling improvements.
Act as the senior escalation point for payment operations.
Key Success Metrics
Dispute win rate and resolution turnaround, owned and improved per processor.
Fraud operations outcomes: fraud loss rate, false positive rate, detection rate, and escalation accuracy.
PSR performance against target across active payment methods and markets, with defined review triggers on all methods.
Incident response and resolution time for publisher-impacting payment issues.
Reporting accuracy, on-time delivery, and operational process maturity as the function scales.
Ideal Profile
6-8+ years in payments operations, fraud ops, or fintech risk, with a track record of owning a function or leading operational initiatives, ideally at a PSP, Merchant of Record, or digital goods company.
Has run these functions end to end, not just participated in them; comfortable operating across multiple payment processors simultaneously, with direct experience of global PSPs such as Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, or Razorpay.
Experience owning PSP or partner relationships and influencing product, engineering, and Customer Success without formal authority.
Deep understanding of dispute and chargeback mechanics at the card network level (Visa/Mastercard rules), not just tool navigation.
Strong analytical capability: works across dashboards and data tools, builds structured reports, and finds signals in noisy transaction data.
Detail-oriented and self-directing; operates with significant autonomy across a broad and growing operational surface.
Business-level English proficiency required, written and verbal.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Alongside our model releases, Anthropic ships a steady stream of launches across the rest of the portfolio — products like Claude, Claude Code, and the developer platform; solutions for enterprises and startups; and the safeguards work that keeps Claude safe and trustworthy. Each launch brings product, engineering, policy, legal, communications, sales, and every part of marketing together around a single moment.
You'll be the central organizer of the product launch process for the product marketing team. You'll treat the launch process itself as a product and drive adoption through influence.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role on a lean product marketing team. When launch volume peaks, you'll contribute directly as a product marketer across all products and surfaces. Own the internal resources our field teams reach for first, along with the operational side of enablement, including scheduling, speakers, and materials logistics
Develop and improve launch processes, playbooks, and operational frameworks that scale beyond any one launch
Own launch retrospectives, recurring product communications, and — when volume requires it — launch materials themselves

Have built or substantially improved a launch or release process
Treat process as a product — you care whether people adopt what you build, and you measure it
Background in product marketing, product operations, technical program management, and launch production all fit

What this job can offer you
You will own and improve the platforms Customer Experience runs on: Zendesk, Vitally, and the integrations that connect them to the rest of the stack.
This is hands-on platform work with real scope. You configure, automate, integrate, and maintain systems used every day by support and customer success teams. You work with autonomy on agreed priorities, use automation (including AI-assisted workflows where they fit), and partner with operations and technical teams when a problem needs more than configuration alone.
You will see work through from scoping to production and ongoing ownership: testing changes, communicating with affected teams, documenting what you ship, and keeping platforms reliable as requirements grow.
How this role contributes to the department's and company's goals
Remote's CX organization depends on reliable tooling: routing that works, automations that hold up under load, and platforms that specialists can trust. This role keeps that foundation solid as the business and product surface area grow.
You will help CX scale without adding friction: fewer manual workarounds, clearer workflows, and platform changes that ship with proper testing, communication, and documentation. Strong platform operations also creates the conditions for automation and AI initiatives to land safely. The work sits close to the teams who use these tools every day, so the impact is direct and measurable.

Strong ownership and autonomy: you spot what needs doing, set direction, and deliver without heavy oversight.
Hands-on Zendesk experience in a production support environment: triggers, automations, views, groups, routing, macros, and comfort debugging via the API when needed.
Platform operations experience in CX or customer success: you understand how support and CSM teams work, not just how admin screens are laid out.
End-to-end delivery: scoping, stakeholder alignment, safe rollout, and steady-state ownership after go-live.
Documentation as part of how you work. Accurate, accessible docs are part of done, not an afterthought.
Sound judgment on when configuration or automation is the right fix, and when the problem needs a different approach.
Automation experience in CX: low/no-code tools (Zapier, platform-native automations, or similar) and workflows that hold up in production.
Practical familiarity with AI in support and success operations: agent assist, workflow automation, triage or routing helpers, or knowledge-backed tools. You do not need to be an ML engineer, but you should be comfortable working with AI-enabled workflows and knowing where they help versus add noise.
Comfort with APIs, webhooks, and integration patterns; able to partner with engineering on harder problems.
Depth in Zendesk or a comparable support platform. Vitally or similar Customer Success platform experience is a strong plus. Willingness to work across more than one system in the stack.
Clear written and spoken English. Remote-first experience is a plus.

Platform administration and reliability
Administer Zendesk, Vitally, and related CX tools: configuration, access, and day-to-day operational health.
Own intake, triage, and delivery for platform requests from internal teams.
Maintain documentation for configurations, automations, and integrations.
Workflow, automation, and AI-enabled tooling
Design and maintain triggers, automations, and data flows that reduce manual handling and keep work moving reliably through CX systems.
Build and run integrations across the CX stack using APIs, webhooks, and low-code tools where that is the right tradeoff.
Identify automation opportunities from ticket data, workflow friction, and team feedback; ship practical improvements, not automation for its own sake.
Support AI-enabled workflows in CX (for example agent assist, routing or triage helpers, and intake automation): configure, test, document, and iterate with appropriate oversight and change control.
Follow change management practices: test before production, communicate impact, document intent and ownership.
Continuous improvement
Use operational data and platform metrics to prioritize work and measure results.
Identify fragile configs, process gaps, and technical debt; address them in a structured way.
Support rollout of new channels, integrations, and workflow changes as CX requirements evolve.

Work with support, success, and operations teams to understand workflow needs and validate solutions before they ship.
Partner with enablement on training and adoption when tooling changes affect frontline teams.
Collaborate with product, engineering, and data teams on integrations and escalations that go beyond platform configuration.

Compliance Operations Analyst - REMOTE

The Compliance Operations Analyst is responsible for supporting Liviniti ’s compliance operations, claim compliance, internal operation audits, and operational oversight functions through audit testing, claims review, data analysis, documentation, reporting, and remediation tracking.

This role assists the Manager of Compliance Operations in evaluating operational accuracy, contractual compliance, regulatory adherence, internal controls, claims processing accuracy, pricing validation, delegated vendor oversight, and fraud, waste, and abuse monitoring activities.

The Compliance Operations Analyst will help execute audit procedures, analyze claims and operational data, document findings, support corrective action follow-up, and contribute to continuous monitoring efforts that strengthen Liviniti ’s compliance posture and operational controls.

The Compliance Operations Analyst is required to perform, but is not limited to, the following responsibilities:
Audit Execution and Claims Review
Own assigned SOC audit activities, including coordination of audit requests, evidence collection, documentation review, status tracking, and follow-up with internal business owners.
Support internal audits related to claims accuracy, pass-through pricing validation, accumulator and benefit setup, claims adjudication, and operational compliance.
Perform claims sampling, testing, and validation in accordance with established audit methodologies, workplans, and review procedures.
Review claims data, system outputs, supporting documentation, SOC control evidence, and operational records to identify discrepancies, trends, or potential control gaps.
Assist with the preparation and maintenance of audit work papers, testing results, evidence files, SOC audit documentation, and supporting materials.
Track SOC audit requests, open items, remediation needs, and management responses to ensure timely completion and audit readiness.
Escalate potential findings, exceptions, control gaps, or risks to the Manager of Compliance Operations for review and direction.
Regulatory and Contractual Compliance Testing
Support testing activities designed to validate adherence to internal policies, regulatory requirements, client contractual obligations, and performance guarantee requirements.
Assist with reviews involving HIPAA/HITECH, ERISA, state PBM transparency requirements, and other applicable compliance obligations as directed.
Compare operational practices, system configurations, and claims outcomes against documented requirements and approved procedures.
Help identify areas where additional review, documentation, corrective action, or process improvement may be needed.
Maintain awareness of assigned regulatory or contractual requirements that impact claims operations, audit scope, and compliance testing
Delegated Vendor Oversight and FWA Support
Assist with delegated vendor audits, third-party oversight reviews, and service-level agreement validation.
Review delegated vendor documentation, performance data, claims activity, and supporting evidence as part of assigned audit procedures.
Support fraud, waste, and abuse review activities by analyzing utilization patterns, claim trends, provider/pharmacy activity, and other data indicators.
Document potential FWA concerns or unusual trends and escalate findings for further review.
Assist with follow-up requests, evidence collection, and tracking related to vendor or FWA review activities.
Reporting, Remediation, and Corrective Action Tracking
Assist in drafting audit summaries, issue logs, testing results, and finding narratives.
Support the development of audit reports that identify observations, findings, risk levels, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.
Maintain remediation trackers and follow up with business owners on assigned corrective and preventative action items.
Validate completion of corrective actions by reviewing supporting documentation and performing follow-up testing as needed.
Prepare status updates, dashboards, and summary materials for review by the Manager of Compliance Operations.
SOP, Governance, and Process Support
Support the development, review, and maintenance of SOPs, work instructions, process documentation, and compliance procedures.
Assist with governance workflows related to audit execution, issue tracking, evidence management, and operational compliance monitoring.
Help organize and maintain audit inventories, documentation repositories, trackers, and supporting files.
Identify opportunities to improve documentation quality, process consistency, and audit readiness.
Participate in process improvement initiatives that strengthen operational controls and compliance oversight.
Dashboarding, Monitoring, and Analytics
Assist with the creation and maintenance of audit dashboards, trackers, reports, and monitoring tools.
Review claims and operational data to identify trends, anomalies, potential compliance risks, or areas requiring additional review.
Support automated sampling, exception reporting, and continuous monitoring efforts in partnership with the Manager of Compliance Operations and Technology teams.
Help compile data-driven insights to support leadership reporting, audit planning, and risk mitigation efforts.

Abide by all obligations under HIPAA related to Protected Health Information and other confidential information.
Report any known or suspected HIPAA violation to the Compliance Officer and/or Human Resources.
Attend, complete, and demonstrate competency in all required HIPAA and compliance training offered by the company.
Maintain discretion, confidentiality, and sound judgment when handling PHI, PII, claims data, client information, and internal business records.
Perform other duties as assigned, with the understanding that responsibilities may change as business needs, compliance requirements, and operational priorities evolve
Required Skills and Competencies
Working knowledge of PBM operations, claims adjudication, benefit design, pricing, network, clinical programs, or healthcare operations.
Understanding of compliance, audit, quality assurance, risk assessment, or internal control concepts.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to review claims data, identify trends, and summarize findings.
Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately document testing results, evidence, and audit conclusions.
Ability to follow established procedures, manage deadlines, and support multiple projects or audits at one time.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize complex information practically and understandably.
High integrity, discretion with PHI/PII, and sound judgment when handling confidential or sensitive information.

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems.
This role will take on new, ambiguous, or underdeveloped operational risks and help mature them into scalable capabilities. We work across USRO and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Legal, Safety, Support, and external vendors or partnership stakeholders.

We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas.
You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process.

You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks.
The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring.

You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop.
Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.
Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.
In This Role, You Will
Take ownership of ambiguous, high-priority safety and risk problems: define the problem, gather the right evidence, choose a practical path, drive execution, and close the loop.
Analyze structured and unstructured data, both quantitative and qualitative. This may include user reports, case narratives, conversations, escalations, and operational metrics to identify patterns, risks, and the highest-leverage interventions.
Build and test lightweight workflows, tools, automations, and decision aids that improve speed, quality, and consistency, then iterate based on real-world use.
Turn one-off insights and manual work into scalable operating mechanisms without adding unnecessary process or complexity.
Lead sensitive investigations, incident response, or launch-readiness work, including safety workflows, human review, escalation paths, partner coordination, and operational monitoring for product launches or cloud deployments.
Work directly with cross-functional and external partners to clarify ownership, resolve operational gaps, and turn incomplete signals into clear recommendations and decisions.
Measure whether the work is improving outcomes—such as quality, speed, coverage, operator effort, or risk reduction—and adjust quickly when it is not.
Help junior operators build judgment and independence through coaching, calibration, and reusable tools.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You
Have 8+ years of experience in trust and safety operations, investigations, incident response, product operations, technical program management, or another high-judgment, data-heavy operational field.
Have a track record as a scrappy generalist who can enter an unfamiliar problem, learn quickly, and deliver with limited structure or support.
Are highly data savvy, including the ability to make sense of messy qualitative or unstructured information and combine it with quantitative evidence.
Are technically fluent and hands-on with AI tools, dashboards, and data tooling, and can build or prototype practical solutions without waiting for a dedicated technical team.
Operate independently, make clear tradeoffs, and maintain momentum as priorities and requirements change.
Think in systems: you look beyond the immediate task and build approaches that can be repeated, measured, and operated by others.
Exercise strong judgment in sensitive situations involving user impact, policy, legal risk, technical constraints, and business priorities.
Communicate clearly and directly, especially in writing, and can drive decisions across teams without formal authority.

Experience in trust and safety, fraud, product safety, integrity, or another adversarial or high-severity risk domain.
Experience moving a new or immature workflow from early investigation into stable, scaled operations.
Experience supporting cloud platforms or deployment partnerships, enterprise products, product launches, connected devices, or other technically complex programs. Direct cloud experience is a plus, not a requirement.
Familiarity with SQL, lightweight scripting, no-code tools, workflow automation, or AI-assisted development.
Experience with vendor operations, quality programs, calibrations, or distributed operational teams.

This is Amplitude's first People Team hire in India, and we're being deliberate about who we bring in first.
People Operations is at an inflection point. A lot of what takes hours today—HR tickets, Workday updates, onboarding tasks—will be handled by AI-assisted workflows in the near future. We're building toward that now, and this role is part of that foundation.

You'll join the global People Operations team as a dedicated shared services resource, handling the operational work that keeps our EMEA and AMER specialists focused on higher-complexity, in-market problems—and supporting People Business Partners globally when they need an extra set of hands.
In the near term, the work is largely transactional: resolving HR helpdesk tickets, processing Workday data requests, coordinating onboarding logistics. That's not a knock on the role—it's the job, and doing it with speed, accuracy, and care matters enormously. Over time, as we invest in AI tooling and automation, that transactional load will shift.

When it does, this role shifts with it: taking on process improvement projects, helping document and refine how the team operates, and growing into a contributor who shapes practices rather than just follows them. We'll support that progression.
Because this is a remote role with no local People Ops team around you, we need someone who is genuinely self-directed. You'll be given clear priorities and good systems to work in, but you'll own your own day. If you thrive in structured work but feel motivated by the promise of doing more over time, this is a good fit.

Own shared services and HR helpdesk

Triage issues that need specialist input—Benefits, Payroll, Legal, or regional People Ops—with clear context and a complete handoff
Hit response SLAs consistently and flag patterns in ticket volume to your team lead
Keep Workday accurate
Process employee lifecycle transactions in Workday on behalf of EMEA and AMER specialists: job changes, compensation updates, terminations, leaves of absence, location changes, and new hire data entry
Conduct regular data quality checks and resolve discrepancies in partnership with regional teams and Payroll
Follow SOX offboarding controls accurately and on time
Support global People Business Partners on request
Handle administrative follow-through on PBP requests: pulling reports, tracking action items, prepping materials, and owning the ops layer so PBPs can stay in their lane
Assist with new hire onboarding coordination—background checks, IT provisioning, welcome logistics—and ensure clean handoffs between TA, IT, and the business
Flag anything requiring compliance, legal, or specialist attention before acting on it yourself
Keep operational needs on track
Provide People Ops support for any India-specific logistics as Amplitude's presence in the country grows
Assist with global employee programs, events, and operational tasks as directed by EMEA and AMER team leads
Help us build better processes over time
Document the work you're doing—not just for records, but to help the team identify what to automate next
Participate in piloting AI-assisted People Ops workflows as they're rolled out
Share feedback on friction points in the work; your day-to-day perspective is how we'll know where to improve

Working closely with, and at the direction of, the Senior Product Operations Manager and Product Leadership team, this role will execute the day-to-day tactics that keep our Product Operating Model running smoothly, while building the experience and judgment to take on greater ownership over time.
Align: work closely with the Product Leadership, Senior Product Operations Manager, Product Managers, and cross-functional business partners to help ensure product work is clearly understood, decisions are communicated effectively, and teams stay aligned on priorities, dependencies, and readiness.
Enable: Help provide product teams with the means to complete routine and strategic tasks as efficiently as possible, by supporting key processes, maintaining tools and workflows, and bringing structure to how work is prepared, reviewed, and tracked.
Improve: Support continuous, iterative improvement of how teams work by helping identify bottlenecks, reducing time spent on non-core product activities, and reinforcing the systems, governance, and operating rhythms that support high-quality product work.

Product Operations is a multifaceted function that focuses on improving how the Product organization operates day to day, driving cross-functional collaboration, and enabling product teams to focus on what they do best: build great products. This role is a mixture of hands-on execution and support for continuous improvement, working under the direction of the Senior Product Operations Manager and Product Leadership team. In this role you will be responsible

Product Operating Model and Product Development Life Cycle (PDLC) Support: Support the flow of work from intake through discovery, assessment, planning, and delivery by helping ensure requests are complete, handoffs are clear, and the right information is available at the right time.
Intake and Initiative Readiness: Support the intake process by serving as a first line of review for incoming requests. Work with stakeholders to gather required inputs and help ensure work is ready for Product review and decision-making.
Operating Rhythm and Meeting Support: Help prepare, coordinate, and, where appropriate, facilitate recurring forums such as Weekly Business Reviews, roadmap reviews, stakeholder meetings, and leadership sessions. Ensure materials are organized, decisions are captured, and follow-up actions are tracked to completion.
Tools and Workflow Optimization: Maintain the product management tech stack, including workflow hygiene, documentation practices, and reporting accuracy, and flag opportunities to improve transparency and usability across Product and cross-functional teams.
Governance and Process Support: Support key operating processes including compliance reviews, cross-functional readiness, and other recurring governance needs that help the business interact effectively with Product.
Cross-functional Project and Program Support: Support the execution of select cross-functional initiatives directed by the Senior Product Operations Manager and Product Managers, helping track alignment on scope, timelines, dependencies, and risks across teams.
Data-informed Execution: Help gather and organize data, reporting, and operational insights to support the Senior Product Operations Manager and Product Leadership in identifying trends and informing process improvements.
Iterative Improvement: Help ensure product operating processes, frameworks, and methodologies remain practical and fit for purpose. Support the rollout of improvements as directed, with a bias toward progress over perfection.
Cross-functional Collaboration: Support open communication and help facilitate alignment between Product, Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Marketing, and other stakeholders, ensuring teams are working effectively toward common goals.
Team Support: Support onboarding, training, and documentation efforts led by the Senior Product Operations Manager and Product Leadership, helping build repeatable ways of working across the Product Organization.

Experience: 2-5 years in product operations, program management, project management, product management, or a similar role, ideally within a technology or product-focused organization.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Equivalent practical experience is also welcomed.
Skill Set
Product Operations is a strategic support function for the business that is as much about coordinating people as it is technology and processes. The strongest candidates will be comfortable owning tactical, day-to-day operational work while building the skills to help identify ways to improve how the organization works over time.
Predominantly, candidates from product operations, program or project management, business operations, product management, business analysis, or similar roles may bring the right mix of execution, organization, and process improvement experience to the position.
An understanding of the full product development lifecycle (PDLC), including intake, discovery, assessment, planning, release, and cross-functional readiness processes.
Works iteratively and pragmatically - eager to help improve the way teams work over time without over-engineering or trying to change everything at once.
A logical and analytical mindset, with a developing ability to understand what can be changed, what value change can bring, and comfort using data to support recommendations.
An empathetic attitude to truly understand the problems you are trying to support and solve with your colleagues and stakeholders.
Comfort with ambiguity, resilience to change, and the ability to adapt while working across multiple priorities and teams.
Experience managing task management and workflow tools - e.g. Jira, Linear, Asana, Productboard, or similar platforms.
Ability to help maintain, organize, and refine knowledge bases and documentation structures using the most suitable information architecture and documentation solution at hand - e.g. Confluence, Notion, etc.
Ability to help use product, process, or operational data to support better decision-making and surface relevant insights from available reporting and analytics.
Experience supporting the administration, adoption, and improvement of software tools and workflows in general.
Comfort supporting meetings and presentations with multiple stakeholders, with growing confidence in facilitating and presenting over time.
Comfort working with all levels of the business - from senior leaders to individual contributors - and a willingness to make suggestions and support positive change under the direction of the Senior Product Operations Manager and Product Leadership.

Prior ownership of experimental initiatives with defined metrics and agile delivery cycles.

The Global Digital Experience team at Uber is responsible for building and scaling enterprise-grade platforms & products that power operations globally. As a Senior Product Operations Manager supporting Platform Integrity, you will own the Product Operations portfolio for a critical operational domain spanning Safety, Risk, Payments, Identity and Compliance for Uber's Community Operations team.
Platform Integrity sits at the center of trust, resilience, and operational excellence across Uber. This role will partner deeply with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and regional Operations teams to intake product needs, translate them into clear problem statements, prioritize them alongside product leaders, and drive disciplined execution from discovery through global rollout and post-launch optimization.
A major focus of this role will be using GenAI, machine learning models, and automation to improve how Platform Integrity products are built, deployed, and scaled. You will help identify where model-enabled workflows can reduce manual effort, improve decision quality, strengthen risk detection, enhance compliance readiness, and create more consistent experiences for internal teams and external users.
This is a high-impact, highly cross-functional role for a strategic operator who can bring structure to ambiguous problem spaces, connect operational pain points to product and platform priorities, and ensure that launches are thoughtful, measurable, globally scalable, and durable across complex regulatory and business contexts.
Success in this role requires strong strategic judgment, systems thinking, analytical depth, executive communication, and the ability to influence without authority across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Operations, Legal, Compliance, Policy, and regional stakeholder groups.
What the Candidate Will Do
Own the strategic Product Operations portfolio for Platform Integrity, spanning Safety, Risk, Payments, Compliance, and related integrity workflows across Global Community Operations.
Build and manage the intake and triage mechanism for Platform Integrity product requests, ensuring requests are clearly defined, supported by data, tied to business outcomes, and evaluated against product strategy, operational urgency, risk exposure, compliance obligations, and customer impact.
Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to prioritize initiatives, sequence roadmap investments, clarify trade-offs, and align stakeholders on what should be built, why it matters, and how success will be measured.
Translate operational insights, regional feedback, model performance signals, support trends, policy changes, compliance requirements, and scalability constraints into clear product requirements, decision frameworks, and executive-ready narratives.
Co-shape the Platform Integrity AI and models roadmap by identifying, validating, and scaling opportunities for GenAI, machine learning, automation, and decision-intelligence capabilities across Safety, Risk, Payments, Identity and Compliance operations.
Partner with Data Science and Product teams to evaluate AI/model use cases, including workflow fit, human-in-the-loop design, escalation paths, quality controls, fairness considerations, operational risk, measurement plans, and post-launch monitoring needs.
Lead structured go-to-market and rollout planning for new Platform Integrity products and capabilities, including readiness planning, stakeholder engagement, documentation, training, change management, launch communications, adoption tracking, and operational support models.
Design and institutionalize scalable operating models, governance mechanisms, feedback loops, and prioritization rituals that improve how Platform Integrity product work is discovered, built, launched, and iterated.
Define and own performance measurement frameworks for launches and ongoing platform health, including adoption, accuracy, efficiency, quality, risk reduction, compliance readiness, defect reduction, and business impact metrics.
Surface post-launch insights, systemic friction points, model gaps, operational defects, and regional adoption barriers to influence roadmap evolution and continuous product improvement.
Serve as the primary Product Operations interface for senior Platform Integrity and Product stakeholders, driving alignment on business priorities, product trade-offs, resourcing decisions, launch risks, and success metrics.
Advise Product, Engineering, and Data Science teams on global feasibility, long-term maintainability, operational durability, regulatory complexity, and supportability of proposed solutions.
Elevate Product Operations standards across the organization by codifying best practices, improving product intake quality, strengthening launch discipline, and creating durable mechanisms that scale beyond individual programs.

Bachelor's degree with a strong record of academic achievement.
6+ years of experience in Product Operations, Product Strategy, Operations, Strategy & Operations, Management Consulting, Program Management, or a similarly analytical and cross-functional role.
Demonstrated experience owning complex, multi-stakeholder portfolios with significant business impact in a scaled product, platform, marketplace, risk, compliance, support, or enterprise environment.
Experience partnering with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and Operations teams to move products from problem discovery through launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration.
Strong analytical fluency, with the ability to independently interrogate data, define measurable success metrics, identify trends, and connect product performance to operational and business outcomes.
Experience leading large-scale, global or multi-region product launches, operational transformations, or change management efforts.
Proven ability to design scalable operating models, governance frameworks, prioritization mechanisms, and feedback loops that create durable operating discipline.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated experience influencing senior stakeholders and driving executive-level alignment in ambiguous, highly matrixed environments.
Strong judgment in operational environments involving safety, risk, payments, compliance, trust, regulatory complexity, or high-volume decisioning workflows.

Experience with AI, GenAI, machine learning models, automation, decision engines, or model-enabled workflows in scaled operational or platform environments.
Familiarity with products or operations related to Safety, Risk, Payments, Compliance, Trust & Safety, Fraud, Identity, Policy, Support Operations, or regulated workflows.
Experience evaluating AI/model use cases, including workflow design, operational controls, model quality measurement, human review, escalation paths, and post-launch monitoring.
Strong business acumen, including the ability to articulate how product and platform decisions impact risk reduction, productivity, quality, compliance readiness, adoption, cost efficiency, and long-term scale.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.
You will own the data Vanta's EPD organization actually runs on — bringing new signal sources online, standardizing them at the point of ingestion, and building the systems that make the underlying data trustworthy rather than merely stored.
The EPD Systems team is building the infrastructure Vanta's engineering, product, and design organization depends on to understand itself. Not by asking teams to be more diligent but by going to the source, processing it, standardizing it, and pushing value back out so each source of truth earns its own adoption.

s.h: What you’ll do as a Operations Manager, Signal Systems at Vanta
s.t:
Bring new signal sources online end to end — from discovery and scoping through ingestion, standardization, and live operation
Identify the specific failure modes in each information source and build systems that mitigate them at the point of ingestion
Go to the teams that produce and consume a signal, understand what the information actually means and what they need back from it, and build accordingly
Replace human-diligence dependencies with engineering solutions: derive fields, pull from source systems, validate at write time
Build alongside teammates who are growing into building — raise their technical ceiling, not just your own output
Partner with the inference and systems layers to ensure what you produce is queryable, trustworthy, and ready to build on

s.h: How to be successful in this role
s.t:
You look at a data source and see its failure modes before its contents: where it lies, where it goes stale, where it's duplicated, where the schema won't hold at 10x
Your first move on an adherence problem is an engineering answer — derive it, pull it, or validate it at write time. Better forms and nudges are your last resort
You've shipped something yourself in roughly the last 12–18 months — a pipeline, an internal tool, a working prototype, an agent — and you can walk through the code and defend your choices. Specs handed to an engineer don't count for this bar
You've built something real with Claude, an LLM API, or agentic tooling — not "I use ChatGPT for drafts." You'll be asked what broke and how you worked around it
You build alongside people: some teammates do program-delivery work today and should grow into building; you see growing their capability as part of your mandate, not a tax on it
You go find out what the data means by talking to the people who produce and consume it, and you come back with a changed understanding — not a requirements list
We use AI to augment our own capabilities and invest deeply in helping every Vantan enhance their work through AI
No CS degree or formal engineering tenure required. Shipping real things fast with AI-assisted tooling clears our bar
Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

We’re Heidi.
We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.
Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.
We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.
If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself then, choose the challenge, choose Heidi.

This is a commercially focused GTM Operations role supporting Heidi’s UK and European markets. You’ll report to the Head of GTM Operations and work closely with leaders across Sales, Customer Success, Marketing and Finance, as well as our central Analytics and GTM Engineering teams.
Your job is to turn commercial direction into an operating model the region can actually use. When leaders agree how we should forecast, segment accounts, organise territories or manage the customer lifecycle, you’ll build the models, processes, reporting and tooling that make it work day to day.
Doing that well means working beyond the CRM. You’ll use HubSpot, Databricks and Omni to bring together commercial and product data, pressure-test assumptions and turn what you find into better decisions and processes.
This role suits someone who enjoys both sides of GTM Operations: working through commercial problems with leaders, then doing the hands-on work to make the solution stick.

Turn commercial plans into working operations. Partner with the Head of GTM Operations and regional leaders to operationalise decisions on segmentation, territories, coverage, capacity, quotas and commissions. Build the models, processes and operating cadences that allow teams to execute them consistently.
Connect the full customer lifecycle. Build and improve the processes between Marketing, Sales and Customer Success, from lead management and pipeline creation through onboarding, adoption, renewal and expansion. Make ownership and handoffs clear, and ensure each team has the information it needs from the others.
Strengthen commercial execution. Improve how we inspect pipeline, forecast revenue and understand customer health, retention and growth. Help embed methodologies such as MEDDIC into the way managers and teams run deals—not just the fields they complete in HubSpot—and drive adoption of the changes you introduce.
Use data to support commercial decisions. Query existing datasets in Databricks, build reporting in Omni and connect CRM, product and commercial data to understand performance. Build the recurring reporting the region needs, investigate issues in more depth when required and explain what changed, why it matters and what action it suggests.
Keep the GTM engine running. Maintain HubSpot and the regional GTM stack, including pipelines, routing, workflows, reporting and data quality. Resolve issues quickly and partner with central teams when something needs a global fix.
What you'll need
Hands-on GTM Operations experience. You’ve worked in GTM Operations, Revenue Operations or Sales Operations and have practical experience with core processes such as forecasting, territory and quota planning, lifecycle management and CRM workflows. We care more about the ownership and judgement you’ve developed than a fixed number of years.
Strong commercial judgement. You can reason across Marketing, Sales and Customer Success, understand the drivers of acquisition, conversion, adoption, retention and expansion, and distinguish an interesting data point from something the business should act on.
Confident with data. You can write SQL, navigate a warehouse such as Databricks and work with a BI tool such as Omni. You’re comfortable interrogating existing datasets, validating the output and turning the result into a clear recommendation. Experience building core warehouse models is not required.
A strong, credible operator. You can take an agreed commercial approach and turn it into a workable model, process or system change. You communicate clearly, challenge assumptions with evidence, bring the right people with you and follow through until the change is adopted.
A practical, tool-fluent systems thinker. You understand how process, data, tooling and team behaviour interact. You’re confident in HubSpot and have worked with tools such as Clay, Gong, outbound platforms, enrichment providers and CPQ/CLM systems, or can get productive in them quickly.
How we show up
Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.
Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.
Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.
Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.
Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.
Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.
Why Heidi?
You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.
Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career.
Equity from day one. When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create.

Die REWAG Entsorgung AG ist ein regional verankertes und unternehmerisch geführtes KMU der Kreislaufwirtschaft in der Nordwestschweiz. Wir sammeln, sortieren, verwerten und bereiten Wertstoffe und Abfälle mit modernen Anlagen fachgerecht auf.
Im Zuge der geplanten Pensionierung unseres langjährigen Betriebsleiters suchen wir per 1\. Januar 2027 oder nach Vereinbarung eine führungsstarke und bodenständige Persönlichkeit als
Betriebsleiter Recycling \& Entsorgung 90–100 %
In dieser Schlüsselposition übernimmst du die operative Führung unserer Betriebe mit Hauptfokus auf Kaiseraugst. Du berichtest direkt an den Geschäftsführer und führst rund 15–20 Mitarbeitende. Du führst nicht vom Büro aus, sondern bist dort präsent, wo der Betrieb läuft. Wenn du Teams mit Respekt und klarer Kante führst und Technik verstehst, bist du bei uns am richtigen Platz.

s.h: Deine Aufgaben – führen, organisieren und weiterentwickeln
s.t:
Betrieb führen: Du führst das operative Tagesgeschäft unserer Standorte mit Hauptfokus Kaiseraugst. Du planst den täglichen Mitarbeiter\- und Maschineneinsatz, setzt Prioritäten und sorgst dafür, dass der Betrieb reibungslos läuft.
Team führen: Du leitest rund 15–20 Mitarbeitende (Platzchef, Maschinisten, Sortier\-/Betriebspersonal, Waage) mit klarer, fairer und verlässlicher Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe.
Materialflüsse koordinieren: Du behältst den Überblick über Annahme, Klassierung, Sortierung, Lagerung und Abtransport unserer Wertstoffe und Abfälle und stellst sicher, dass Materialien zur richtigen Zeit am richtigen Ort sind.
Betrieb weiterentwickeln: Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenziale in Abläufen, Organisation und Technik und setzt diese gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung pragmatisch um.
Maschinenpark im Schuss halten: Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Bagger, Radlader, Stapler, Pressen, Schredder sowie Aufbereitungs\- und Sortieranlagen einsatzbereit, gewartet und gepflegt sind. Grössere Reparaturen sprichst du mit externen Partnern ab.
Platz \& Sicherheit: Du schaust auf Sauberkeit, Struktur und Ordnung auf dem gesamten Areal und setzt Sicherheits\-, Umwelt\- und Brandschutzregeln konsequent durch.
Verantwortung übernehmen: Du vertrittst den Geschäftsführer bei Abwesenheit und bringst deine Ideen bei Neuanschaffungen und Projekten ein.
Das bringst du mit – Führung, Technik und gesunder Menschenverstand:
Berufsausbildung: Abgeschlossene technische, handwerkliche oder vergleichbare Berufsausbildung.
Weiterbildung: Eine Weiterbildung zum Technischen , Prozessfachmann, Betriebsfachmann oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation ist von Vorteil.
Führungserfahrung: Führungserfahrung in einem operativen Umfeld mit unterschiedlich qualifizierten Mitarbeitenden ist besonders willkommen. Du kommunizierst direkt, respektvoll, klar und lässt dich auch in hektischen Momenten nicht aus der Ruhe bringen.
Hands\-on\-Mentalität: Du packst Probleme pragmatisch an, entscheidest und organisierst gerne und bist im Betrieb sichtbar und präsent.
Wohnort: Dein Wohnort ermöglicht dir eine zuverlässige Präsenz in Kaiseraugst.
Führerschein: Führerausweis Kat. B ist Pflicht; Baumaschinenausweis und/oder Maschinistenpraxis sind ein Plus.
Branchenerfahrung: Erfahrung im Recycling\-, Schüttgut\- oder Baustellenbereich ist von Vorteil – motivierte Quereinsteiger mit solider Führungspraxis sind willkommen!

Viel Freiraum: Hohe Eigenverantwortung und echtes Vertrauen in deine tägliche Arbeit.
Schlüsselposition: Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Geschäftsführer zusammen und kannst den Betrieb aktiv mitgestalten.
Abwechslungsreicher Betrieb: Unterschiedliche Materialien, Maschinen, Anlagen und Standorte sorgen dafür, dass kein Tag genau gleich aussieht.
Sicherer Arbeitsplatz: Ein wirtschaftlich gesundes, regional verankertes KMU mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen und langjährigen Mitarbeitenden.
Moderne Technik: Gute Maschinen und zeitgemässe Recyclinganlagen.
Klare Verantwortlichkeiten: Administration, ISO\-System, Budgetierung und Fuhrparkmanagement werden durch andere Stellen unterstützt bzw. verantwortet – du kannst dich auf die operative Führung der Betriebe konzentrieren.
Zeitgemässe Anstellungsbedingungen: 5 Wochen Ferien, gute Sozialleistungen und faire, marktgerechte Anstellungsbedingungen.
Bereit für den nächsten Schritt?
Sende uns deine Bewerbung bitte direkt. Deine Bewerbung behandeln wir selbstverständlich vertraulich. Auf die Bewerbungsadresse hat ausschliesslich der Geschäftsführer Zugriff.
(Hinweis: Wir berücksichtigen ausschliesslich Direktbewerbungen. Dossiers von Personalvermittlern können wir nicht bearbeiten.)
